---
name: project-sfcc237-mrt-topology-spike
description: SFCC-237 spike — MRT app topology TSD (single vs per-integration MRT apps); full research pass 2026-08-10 with root-caused discrepancies, template clarification, and remaining human-only open items
metadata:
  type: project
---

SFCC-237 ("Spike: MRT Application Architecture Strategy (Single vs Per-Integration MRT Apps)",
3 pts, label Squad-A, epic SFCC-1 "Platform Setup & Environments", assignee me/Marcel Angelo
Navarro, reporter Hazel Marie Cacalda) — **due date 2026-08-10 (today), already slipped 4x
(08-03→06→07→10); today is also SFCC Sprint 2's last day (2026-07-28→2026-08-10).** DoD: a TSD
comparing Option A (single app) vs Option B (per-integration app) vs a middle option (single
modular app), scored on deploy/rollback, failure isolation (event-loop/memory/process, not just
sockets), secrets/security blast radius, performance/LCP, cost, ownership — with an agreed as-is
baseline, a recommendation, and Technical Lead (Tim) sign-off. Tim asked me + Gideon R. Linsangan
(SFCC squad; currently active on SFCC-241 "Validate MuleSoft Sync Process") to collaborate. No
linked branches/PRs/commits on the ticket (pure docs deliverable). Complements
[[project-spike-122-123-audit]] (SFCC-122 = what MRT can *consume*, Done; this = how many MRT apps
we *deploy*).

## Deliverable format — do NOT reuse tsd-architecture.md's structure

Must follow the official 8-section TSD template (Confluence page 352419841 — see
[[project-tsd-templates]]: Document Info → 1 Problem Statement → 2 Constraints & Assumptions →
3 Options Analysis → 4 Recommended Option & Rationale → 5 Technical Implementation →
6 Testing & Validation → 7 Risks & Mitigations → 8 Decision Record/sign-off), governed by Tim's
"one TSD = one problem" rule. `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md` (581 lines, "Technical Solution
Design — PWA (Architecture)", content last substantively touched 2026-07-16) is a *different*,
older, pre-template document covering the whole PWA architecture — it is **background/baseline
source material** for this TSD (its §12.1 Blast-Radius Containment and §14 CI/CD & Environments
are directly relevant), **not** the SFCC-237 deliverable itself. Its own §14 opens with "this
section probably belongs to a DevOps TSD... temporarily until we have one" — it already
self-identifies as a placeholder pending exactly this kind of proper split-out. `.docs/temp/
openItems.md` (companion file, 18-integration open-items register) has nothing on MRT app count —
its items are all per-vendor credentials/contracts, not deploy topology.

## As-is baseline — fully re-verified 2026-08-10 against live codebase (not just docs)

- **One PWA Kit project**, slug `zimmermann` (from `package.json`'s `"name"` field), **six push
  targets** (`npm run push:{dev,test,sit,uat,staging,prod}` → `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`),
  each bound to its own GitHub Environment + `deploy-*.yml`, all deploying the *same* build
  artifact. Today's only deploy-topology axis is **environment tier**, not integration domain.
  Repo-wide grep for "per-integration", "per-app", "MRT app(lication)", "multiple MRT" = **0 hits
  everywhere** — SFCC-237 is genuinely greenfield analysis; nothing in the repo pre-empts or
  contradicts any of the three options.
- Only **2 proxy origins** configured in *every* tier's config (`config/default.js`
  `ssrParameters.proxyConfigs`, spread + host-overridden per tier): SCAPI + OCAPI. No
  mulesoft/google/booxi proxy entries exist anywhere in `config/` yet — consistent with most of
  the ~18 `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` systems (confirmed still exactly 18 numbered files + index.md,
  unchanged since 07-30 except two content-only edits to `02-contentful.md`) not having code built
  yet (sprintScope.md).
- `.docs/prd/regional.md` and `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md` — read in full, both silent on MRT
  app topology (only environment-*tier* language). Nothing to reconcile.
- CODEOWNERS Tier-1-protects `config/`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `overrides/app/ssr/`,
  `worker/main.js`, `mobify.config.js` (stale, see below), `.github/workflows/` — all
  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.

## Discrepancy #1 (mobify.config.js) — CONFIRMED absent + root-caused 2026-08-10

Still doesn't exist as a file, and `package.json` has no `"mobify"` key either. Traced the actual
mechanism in the installed `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev@3.18.0` / `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime@3.18.0`
(both pulled transitively via `retail-react-app@10.0.0` — root `package.json` doesn't pin them
directly): `bin/pwa-kit-dev.js:395` calls `getConfig()` (from `pwa-kit-runtime/utils/
ssr-config.server.js:59-75`), which uses `cosmiconfig` searching, in order,
`config/{DEPLOY_TARGET}.js` → `config/local.js` → `config/default.js` → `package.json`'s `mobify`
key. **A root `mobify.config.js` file is never in this version's search path at all** — this isn't
a missing file, it's a stale reference to a mechanism this PWA Kit version doesn't use. Project
slug (`zimmermann`) actually comes from `package.json`'s `"name"` via `getProjectName()`.

Now cited as real in **seven** places (was 3 at the 07-30 pass): `.docs/architecture.md:108`,
`.docs/memory/projectState.md:24`, `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md:55` (**Tier 1**),
`CODEOWNERS:50` (**Tier 1**), `.github/copilot-instructions.md:388`,
`.docs/prompts/omsIntClaudeCodePrompt.md` (×2), **and now confirmed on Confluence too** — "05.6 -
Environment Details" (285540356): "MRT push credentials... scoped to the project slug in
`mobify.config.js`." Fixing this touches Tier-1 *Governance* files (frozenFiles.md, CODEOWNERS),
which AGENTS.md's own footer requires both squad leads + Integration lead to approve — flagged to
the user, not spawned as an autonomous background fix. See
[[project-env-topology-doc-conflicts]] conflicts #6/#9 for the Confluence-side sibling finding.

## Discrepancy #2 (undici pools inert) — CONFIRMED still fully inert 2026-08-10

`overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts` still defines the same 7 pools (`sfcc-scapi`,
`sfcc-payments`, `mulesoft`, `marketing-cloud-auth`, `marketing-cloud-rest`, `google-places`,
`booxi`). Zero imports/usages anywhere else in `overrides/` (grep-confirmed across the whole
tree). All 4 real SSR `fetch()` calls (`slasTokens.ts:78`, `paymentMetadata.ts:42-44`,
`marketingCloud.ts:38-46,61-75`) use the bare global dispatcher, no `dispatcher` option passed.
Git history proves this was never wired, not just "not yet caught up": the file has exactly **one
commit ever** (`610020e`, the original `ssr.js`→`ssr/` split), zero follow-ups, and — per
`git log --since=2026-07-30` — zero commits to `worker/main.js`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`,
`overrides/app/ssr/`, or `CODEOWNERS` at all in the last 11 days. `overrides/app/
request-processor.js` is confirmed still the unmodified Salesforce example stub (still contains
the template's own "this is an EXAMPLE file" comment). `worker/main.js` is a 7-line
license-header-only stub with no logic.

**Correction to the ticket's own Background text:** it states today's isolation is "at the network
level via per-origin `undici` connection pools" — that overstates reality. The pools are *designed*
but not wired, so today's real isolation is **zero**: all integrations share one global `fetch`
dispatcher in one process. Worth correcting in the TSD's as-is baseline rather than repeating the
ticket's own premise verbatim.

## Governance implication for whatever this TSD recommends

Implementing any topology change will eventually touch `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`,
`overrides/app/ssr.js`, and/or `worker/main.js` — all four are **absolute** Tier-1 files under
AGENTS.md Hard Rule #4 (no verified-session/tier-1-approver exception applies to these specific
four, unlike ordinary Tier 1 files). Not blocking for *writing* the TSD (docs-only), but worth a
flag in the TSD's §5 Technical Implementation so the eventual build-out isn't surprised by it.

## Open items that genuinely cannot be resolved from any available source

Checked codebase, all repo docs, Confluence (including a fresh search), and JIRA — none document:
(1) whether MRT supports multiple independent apps/projects in Zimmermann's org; (2) a cost/
licensing model per environment/app (no Confluence page covers this — checked); (3) the MRT
execution/concurrency model and real failure blast radius. These require Gideon and/or the
platform team directly, exactly as the ticket's own task list says — do not guess them, they are
undocumented anywhere, not just hard to find.

## Related people/tickets confirmed live 2026-08-10

Gideon Linsangan (SFCC-241, MuleSoft sync spike, In Progress — his MuleSoft work is directly
relevant since `mulesoft` is the highest-connection-pool-cap pool in §12.1 and a key input to any
per-integration boundary discussion). Manikandan Ramachandran owns epic SFCC-1. SFCC-254
("Environment Setup DEV/TEST/SIT/UAT") is now assigned to **me** per live JIRA (a prior memory had
it on Victor Crisostomo — that's stale, trust this live check) and structurally sequences after
this ticket's topology decision. SFCC-249 (Contentful TSD redo, Code Review, Jhoan) cross-
references "SFCC-237 — TSD in progress" in its own Confluence page (346783750) as a dependency
note, not a shared deliverable.

**Why:** re-verified everything from the 07-30 pass plus went deeper (node_modules tracing,
Confluence Test-tier cross-check, full JIRA ticket text + changelog, fresh grep sweep). Every
prior finding held up and several got sharper root causes; nothing has changed in the underlying
files (git log confirms zero commits to the flagged files since 07-30).
**How to apply:** the as-is baseline section of the TSD can be written now, fully sourced from this
memory. The options analysis / recommendation (§3-4) genuinely cannot be finalised without the
Gideon/platform conversation above — surface that to the user before drafting those sections
rather than guessing at platform capability or cost.

+self-identifies as a placeholder pending exactly this kind of proper split-out. `.docs/temp/
+openItems.md` (companion file, 18-integration open-items register) has nothing on MRT app count —
+its items are all per-vendor credentials/contracts, not deploy topology.
-**Architectural crux for the options:** MRT hosts one PWA Kit bundle per project; the SSR render composes
-many integrations in one request and can't be split across apps. Option B realistically only applies to
-server-side proxy/webhook/API endpoints, which are still session/cookie/CSP-coupled to the render.
-undici pools give socket isolation within one app but NOT event-loop/memory/process isolation — a separate
-app/process would. That's the genuine tradeoff.
+## As-is baseline — fully re-verified 2026-08-10 against live codebase (not just docs)
-**Open items needing Gideon/Mani/platform (do NOT guess):** (1) does MRT support multiple independent
-apps/projects in Zimmermann's org; (2) cost model per environment/app; (3) MRT execution/concurrency model
-+ real failure blast radius.
+- **One PWA Kit project**, slug `zimmermann` (from `package.json`'s `"name"` field), **six push
+  targets** (`npm run push:{dev,test,sit,uat,staging,prod}` → `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`),
+  each bound to its own GitHub Environment + `deploy-*.yml`, all deploying the *same* build
+  artifact. Today's only deploy-topology axis is **environment tier**, not integration domain.
+  Repo-wide grep for "per-integration", "per-app", "MRT app(lication)", "multiple MRT" = **0 hits
+  everywhere** — SFCC-237 is genuinely greenfield analysis; nothing in the repo pre-empts or
+  contradicts any of the three options.
+- Only **2 proxy origins** configured in *every* tier's config (`config/default.js`
+  `ssrParameters.proxyConfigs`, spread + host-overridden per tier): SCAPI + OCAPI. No
+  mulesoft/google/booxi proxy entries exist anywhere in `config/` yet — consistent with most of
+  the ~18 `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` systems (confirmed still exactly 18 numbered files + index.md,
+  unchanged since 07-30 except two content-only edits to `02-contentful.md`) not having code built
+  yet (sprintScope.md).
+- `.docs/prd/regional.md` and `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md` — read in full, both silent on MRT
+  app topology (only environment-*tier* language). Nothing to reconcile.
+- CODEOWNERS Tier-1-protects `config/`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `overrides/app/ssr/`,
+  `worker/main.js`, `mobify.config.js` (stale, see below), `.github/workflows/` — all
+  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.
-**Why:** this is Angelo's active spike; the as-is facts and the two discrepancies took a full codebase +
-Confluence pass to establish and aren't obvious from any single file.
-**How to apply:** start the TSD from these facts; raise the 3 open items with Gideon before writing §4
-recommendation; correct the stale mobify.config.js references as part of the work.
+## Discrepancy #1 (mobify.config.js) — CONFIRMED absent + root-caused 2026-08-10
+Still doesn't exist as a file, and `package.json` has no `"mobify"` key either. Traced the actual
+mechanism in the installed `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev@3.18.0` / `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime@3.18.0`
+(both pulled transitively via `retail-react-app@10.0.0` — root `package.json` doesn't pin them
+directly): `bin/pwa-kit-dev.js:395` calls `getConfig()` (from `pwa-kit-runtime/utils/
+ssr-config.server.js:59-75`), which uses `cosmiconfig` searching, in order,
+`config/{DEPLOY_TARGET}.js` → `config/local.js` → `config/default.js` → `package.json`'s `mobify`
+key. **A root `mobify.config.js` file is never in this version's search path at all** — this isn't
+a missing file, it's a stale reference to a mechanism this PWA Kit version doesn't use. Project
+slug (`zimmermann`) actually comes from `package.json`'s `"name"` via `getProjectName()`.
+Now cited as real in **seven** places (was 3 at the 07-30 pass): `.docs/architecture.md:108`,
+`.docs/memory/projectState.md:24`, `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md:55` (**Tier 1**),
+`CODEOWNERS:50` (**Tier 1**), `.github/copilot-instructions.md:388`,
+`.docs/prompts/omsIntClaudeCodePrompt.md` (×2), **and now confirmed on Confluence too** — "05.6 -
+Environment Details" (285540356): "MRT push credentials... scoped to the project slug in
+`mobify.config.js`." Fixing this touches Tier-1 *Governance* files (frozenFiles.md, CODEOWNERS),
+which AGENTS.md's own footer requires both squad leads + Integration lead to approve — flagged to
+the user, not spawned as an autonomous background fix. See
+[[project-env-topology-doc-conflicts]] conflicts #6/#9 for the Confluence-side sibling finding.
+## Discrepancy #2 (undici pools inert) — CONFIRMED still fully inert 2026-08-10
+`overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts` still defines the same 7 pools (`sfcc-scapi`,
+`sfcc-payments`, `mulesoft`, `marketing-cloud-auth`, `marketing-cloud-rest`, `google-places`,
+`booxi`). Zero imports/usages anywhere else in `overrides/` (grep-confirmed across the whole
+tree). All 4 real SSR `fetch()` calls (`slasTokens.ts:78`, `paymentMetadata.ts:42-44`,
+`marketingCloud.ts:38-46,61-75`) use the bare global dispatcher, no `dispatcher` option passed.
+Git history proves this was never wired, not just "not yet caught up": the file has exactly **one
+commit ever** (`610020e`, the original `ssr.js`→`ssr/` split), zero follow-ups, and — per
+`git log --since=2026-07-30` — zero commits to `worker/main.js`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`,
+`overrides/app/ssr/`, or `CODEOWNERS` at all in the last 11 days. `overrides/app/
+request-processor.js` is confirmed still the unmodified Salesforce example stub (still contains
+the template's own "this is an EXAMPLE file" comment). `worker/main.js` is a 7-line
+license-header-only stub with no logic.
+**Correction to the ticket's own Background text:** it states today's isolation is "at the network
+level via per-origin `undici` connection pools" — that overstates reality. The pools are *designed*
+but not wired, so today's real isolation is **zero**: all integrations share one global `fetch`
+dispatcher in one process. Worth correcting in the TSD's as-is baseline rather than repeating the
+ticket's own premise verbatim.
+## Governance implication for whatever this TSD recommends
+Implementing any topology change will eventually touch `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`,
+`overrides/app/ssr.js`, and/or `worker/main.js` — all four are **absolute** Tier-1 files under
+AGENTS.md Hard Rule #4 (no verified-session/tier-1-approver exception applies to these specific
+four, unlike ordinary Tier 1 files). Not blocking for *writing* the TSD (docs-only), but worth a
+flag in the TSD's §5 Technical Implementation so the eventual build-out isn't surprised by it.
+## Open items that genuinely cannot be resolved from any available source
+Checked codebase, all repo docs, Confluence (including a fresh search), and JIRA — none document:
+(1) whether MRT supports multiple independent apps/projects in Zimmermann's org; (2) a cost/
+licensing model per environment/app (no Confluence page covers this — checked); (3) the MRT
+execution/concurrency model and real failure blast radius. These require Gideon and/or the
+platform team directly, exactly as the ticket's own task list says — do not guess them, they are
+undocumented anywhere, not just hard to find.
+## Related people/tickets confirmed live 2026-08-10
+Gideon Linsangan (SFCC-241, MuleSoft sync spike, In Progress — his MuleSoft work is directly
+relevant since `mulesoft` is the highest-connection-pool-cap pool in §12.1 and a key input to any
+per-integration boundary discussion). Manikandan Ramachandran owns epic SFCC-1. SFCC-254
+("Environment Setup DEV/TEST/SIT/UAT") is now assigned to **me** per live JIRA (a prior memory had
+it on Victor Crisostomo — that's stale, trust this live check) and structurally sequences after
+this ticket's topology decision. SFCC-249 (Contentful TSD redo, Code Review, Jhoan) cross-
+references "SFCC-237 — TSD in progress" in its own Confluence page (346783750) as a dependency
+note, not a shared deliverable.
+**Why:** re-verified everything from the 07-30 pass plus went deeper (node_modules tracing,
+Confluence Test-tier cross-check, full JIRA ticket text + changelog, fresh grep sweep). Every
+prior finding held up and several got sharper root causes; nothing has changed in the underlying
+files (git log confirms zero commits to the flagged files since 07-30).
+**How to apply:** the as-is baseline section of the TSD can be written now, fully sourced from this
+memory. The options analysis / recommendation (§3-4) genuinely cannot be finalised without the
+Gideon/platform conversation above — surface that to the user before drafting those sections
+rather than guessing at platform capability or cost.

SFCC-237 (Spike, assigned to Angelo; epic SFCC-1 Platform Setup; In Progress) — deliverable is a
**TSD** comparing MRT (Managed Runtime) application topology: **Option A** single MRT app for all
integrations (current default), **Option B** dedicated MRT app per integration/domain, **+ middle**
single modular app. Scored on deploy/rollback, failure isolation (event-loop/memory/process, not just
sockets), secrets/security blast radius, performance/LCP, cost, ownership. Tim asked Angelo (FED) +
Gideon (SFCC) to collaborate; needs Technical Lead sign-off (§8). Complements [[project-spike-122-123-audit]]
(SFCC-122 = what MRT can *consume*; this = how many MRT apps we *deploy*). Uses official 8-section TSD
template — see [[project-tsd-templates]].

**As-is baseline (confirmed code + Confluence, verify before quoting):**
- Single MRT application (PWA Kit project named `zimmermann`), one Express handler `overrides/app/ssr.js`,
  one MRT project with per-tier **environment** targets (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/production) — NOT
  per-integration apps. Confluence 05.6 (285540356): MRT apps `zimmermann-<tier>`, project slug
  `sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1`. Deploy = `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>` (`package.json`), one GH workflow per tier.
- Only **2 proxy origins per env today**: SCAPI (`/mobify/proxy/api`, host `qmyt7hks...`) + OCAPI
  (`/mobify/proxy/ocapi`, per-tier host) in `config/*.js` `ssrParameters.proxyConfigs`. No
  mulesoft/google/booxi proxy entries yet.
- The "~18 systems" = the 18 numbered `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` files (PWA-layer integrations only;
  excludes SFCC↔MuleSoft backend). Most have **no code footprint yet** — land in later sprints
  (`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`); current position Sprint 0.

**Two discrepancies found (flag in TSD):**
1. **`mobify.config.js` does not exist in the repo**, yet `.docs/architecture.md:108`, the TSD draft
   §14.4, and `.docs/memory/projectState.md:24` all reference it as where MRT targets map. MRT targeting
   is actually via `pwa-kit-dev push -t` + per-tier `config/*.js`. (Note: it's also listed Tier 1 in
   frozenFiles.md.)
2. **Blast-radius isolation is inert scaffolding.** `overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts` defines 7
   per-origin `undici` pools documented against TSD §12.1, but they are **imported nowhere** and
   `dispatcher` is attached to no real `fetch()`. Actual SSR fetches (`slasTokens.ts`, `paymentMetadata.ts`,
   `marketingCloud.ts`) use the global dispatcher. So the ticket's premise ("isolates only at network
   level via per-origin undici pools") overstates today's state — even socket isolation isn't wired yet.
   `request-processor.js` is still the Salesforce example stub.

**Architectural crux for the options:** MRT hosts one PWA Kit bundle per project; the SSR render composes
many integrations in one request and can't be split across apps. Option B realistically only applies to
server-side proxy/webhook/API endpoints, which are still session/cookie/CSP-coupled to the render.
undici pools give socket isolation within one app but NOT event-loop/memory/process isolation — a separate
app/process would. That's the genuine tradeoff.

**Open items needing Gideon/Mani/platform (do NOT guess):** (1) does MRT support multiple independent
apps/projects in Zimmermann's org; (2) cost model per environment/app; (3) MRT execution/concurrency model
+ real failure blast radius.

**Why:** this is Angelo's active spike; the as-is facts and the two discrepancies took a full codebase +
Confluence pass to establish and aren't obvious from any single file.
**How to apply:** start the TSD from these facts; raise the 3 open items with Gideon before writing §4
recommendation; correct the stale mobify.config.js references as part of the work.

- **One MRT project** (`zimmermann`), **six environment-tier push targets** (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), all deploying the same build. Today's only deploy axis is environment, not integration domain.

## In-depth analysis: SFCC-237

### Timeline reconstruction (from the changelog)
Created 2026-07-24 (Hazel) → Ready for Development 07-28 → **you moved it to In Progress 07-30, same day Start Date was set** → story points bumped 2→3 (07-27, before you started) → due date pushed four times, all by Hazel: (unset)→08-03→08-06→08-07→**08-10 (today)**. Zero comments on the ticket. Today's only other change is the RemoteWorkItemLink (almost certainly an incidental Jira-macro backlink from Jhoan's SFCC-249 Confluence page, which name-drops "SFCC-237 — TSD in progress" as a dependency note — not a new artifact for this ticket).

### Objective — precise parse
"Produce a TSD comparing two approaches for structuring the storefront's MRT Node layer **as integrations are built out**... so the squad makes a deliberate, signed-off decision on deployment topology **before the integration build-out hardens it**." The urgency driver isn't the due date — it's that this becomes expensive to retrofit once integration code exists. Right now almost none does (18 systems, near-zero built), which is exactly why the ticket exists *now*.

### Background — one factual correction worth carrying into the TSD
The ticket's own text says today's isolation is "at the network level (per-origin `undici` connection pools)." My verification shows that's slightly too generous: the pools are *defined* but have zero imports anywhere and every real SSR fetch uses the bare global dispatcher. **Actual isolation today is none, not network-level.** This is a stronger, more accurate Problem Statement fact than the ticket text itself — I'd use my verified version in §1.2, not restate the ticket verbatim.

### Task-by-task: what's answerable now vs. genuinely Gideon/platform-only
Re-reading the Tasks list against everything already verified:

| Task | Resolvable now? |
|---|---|
| Baseline: single MRT app, proxies wired, in-process isolation, cartridge/MRT-mediated/SFCC→MuleSoft boundary, deploy/secret model | **Yes** — fully code/doc-confirmed |
| Baseline: **platform limits** | **No** — undocumented anywhere |
| MRT multi-app support in our org + **cost model per environment/app** | **No** — undocumented anywhere, explicit Gideon/platform task |
| Options comparison (deploy/rollback, failure isolation, secrets/security, LCP, cost, ownership) | **Partially** — qualitative architecture reasoning is doable now; the cost axis and the concurrency-driven part of failure isolation are contingent on the two items above |
| MRT execution/concurrency model & blast-radius effect | **No** — nothing documents this |
| Recommendation tied to constraints | **Contingent** on the above two "No" rows — a provisional recommendation is possible now, but if MRT literally can't run multiple independent apps on this org's licence, Option B is dead regardless of how its tradeoffs score on paper |
| Capture in TSD + Tim sign-off | Mechanical once the above settles |

The Background text itself is explicit that this ordering matters: *"the as-is baseline is to be confirmed with Gideon/platform before the options analysis."* That's not my inference — it's written into the ticket.

### Template — confirmed via direct fetch (not memory)
`/wiki/x/AYABFQ` decodes to and fetches identically to page **352419841, "Technical Solution Document (TSD) Template," v2**. Exact 8-section structure captured verbatim in memory now (Document Info + Version History → 1 Problem Statement → 2 Constraints & Assumptions → 3 Options Analysis → 4 Recommended Option & Rationale → 5 Technical Implementation → 6 Testing & Validation → 7 Risks & Mitigations → 8 Decision Record + sign-off), including the instructional callouts I'll hold to strictly — notably: §1 must contain zero solution/options content, §3 must list a "do nothing"/discarded option too, §5 is chosen-option-only and must not restate §3, and §7's "no risks identified" is flagged on the template itself as almost never a valid answer.

### The tension this creates
Sections 1, 2, 5 (partly), 6, and 7 can be drafted now from verified fact. Sections 3, 4, and the "agreed" baseline in the Doc Info can only be marked **Draft** with Gideon's two answers (multi-app support + cost, concurrency model) still open — the DoD literally requires an "agreed" baseline and the template's own header says a TSD isn't approved until §8 sign-off anyway, so a Draft with explicit open items is a normal, valid state for this template, not a broken one.

content.content:
1	# Managed Runtime Overview
2	
3	[Managed Runtime](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.md) provides the infrastructure to deploy, host, and monitor your PWA Kit storefront.
4	
5	:::important
6	Managed Runtime only supports applications created from a PWA Kit template. The source code for the available templates can be found in the `template-*` folders in the [PWA Kit repository](https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/tree/develop/packages) on GitHub.
7	:::
8	
9	This guide covers the main parts of Managed Runtime and how to access it.
10	
11	::include{src="../../shared/managed-runtime-access.md"}
12	
13	:::important
14	Before you can use Managed Runtime and Runtime Admin, ask your B2C Commerce administrator to add one of these roles to your account in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.
15	:::
16	
17	## Environments
18	
19	An **environment** is the term used to describe all of the cloud infrastructure and configuration values for a particular storefront hosted by Managed Runtime. Environments are used to separate your production storefront from other storefronts that are deployed for other purposes, such as development or testing.
20	
21	:::note
22	In the [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary), environments are called “targets,” but both terms refer to the same thing.
23	:::
24	
25	Because environments run on highly efficient microservices that automatically scale up and down, you can create as many environments as you need at no additional cost. For example, you could create a short-lived environment dedicated to a single agile development sprint or for a single user story within that sprint. When you no longer need an environment, we encourage you to delete them.
26	
27	### Production Environments
28	
29	Environments marked as production are prioritized for monitoring by Salesforce’s Support team. For production environments, you can also [Debug Using Log Center](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/debugging.html#debug-using-log-center). To mark an environment as a production, you have two choices:
30	
31	1. Use the Runtime Admin tool. Step-by-step instructions for creating an environment or editing an existing environment are found in the [Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#environments) section of the Administration guide.
32	2. Use the Managed Runtime API. The [projects_target_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_create) and [projects_target_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_partial_update) endpoints both feature the `is_production` parameter. To mark an environment as production with these endpoints, set `is_production` to `true`.
33	
34	:::important
35	By default, you can mark up to 10 environments as production. To increase your limit, contact Support.
36	:::
37	
38	## Bundles
39	
40	The storefront code that runs on an environment is called a **bundle**. Use the developer tools included in PWA Kit to generate a bundle and push it to Managed Runtime.
41	
42	:::note
43	A bundle is a snapshot of your code at a specific point in time. It’s *immutable*: After a bundle has been created, it can’t be changed. Having this complete and accurate history of bundles makes troubleshooting deployments easier.
44	:::
45	
46	After pushing the bundle, you can use the Runtime Admin or Managed Runtime API to designate that bundle as “deployed.” Each project can have multiple bundles, but each environment can have only one bundle that's designated as deployed. You can change which bundle is designated as deployed at any time. For more information, see [Push and Deploy Bundles](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/pushing-and-deploying-bundles.md).
47	
48	## Projects and Organizations
49	
50	To help you manage multiple environments, each environment also belongs to a **project** and each project belongs to an **organization**. An organization can contain multiple projects for multiple storefronts and each project can contain multiple environments. A Managed Runtime user can belong to multiple organizations to separate different work streams.
51	
52	Each organization can have a maximum of 100 total environments and a maximum of 10 production environments. If you need to raise these limits, contact your Salesforce Support representative.
53	
54	Organizations and user organization membership is determined by settings in Account Manager. A user can belong to an organization as either a member or an admin. Members can only interact with the projects in Managed Runtime that they’ve been assigned a project role to. Admins can interact with all the projects within an organization.
55	
56	:::important
57	To assign a user the admin organization membership, contact Salesforce Support.
58	:::
59	
60	## Users, Abilities, and Roles
61	
62	All users must be assigned the `Managed Runtime User` or `Managed Runtime Admin` via [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com) for accessing Managed Runtime.
63	
64	### Organization Roles and Permissions
65	
66	Any user can have the following capabilities for a Managed Runtime organization:
67	
68	- **Browse:** View all projects for an Organization.
69	- **Certificate:** View or manage TLS Certificates for an organization.
70	
71	### Project Roles and Permissions
72	
73	Any user can have the following capabilities for a Managed Runtime project:
74	
75	- **Browse:** View the project in Runtime Admin.
76	- **Manage Redirects:** Manage redirects for the project. Please review the [Redirects documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html?q=Redirects#redirects) to learn more.
77	- **Deploy:** Deploy new bundles or revert the deployment to an older bundle.
78	- **Manage Team:** View, add, invite, remove, and edit the roles of team members for the project.
79	- **Access Logs:** Tail logs across all environments.

82	Each user is assigned a project role that determines which abilities they have. (A user can only have *one* role.) Project roles can be assigned to any user within an organization.

92	
93	## App Server
94	
95	Within each Managed Runtime environment, the [React](https://reactjs.org/) app in the published bundle runs inside a [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) environment. To respond to page requests and render the results, we use the [Express](https://expressjs.com/) web framework with the help of PWA Kit’s [rendering](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/rendering.md) and [routing](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/routing.md) systems. We call this combination of React, Node, and Express the **App Server**. (Although, technically speaking, the App Server runs on “serverless” technology.) The App Server is optimized to run on cloud infrastructure that offers low computing costs, high availability, fast rendering, and massive scaling capacity.
96	
97	Because PWA Kit’s rendering and routing system handles the differences between local development environments and Managed Runtime environments, your code runs in a predictable way when you deploy it. This predictability unlocks your development team’s productivity by encouraging them to deploy bundles more frequently.
98	
99	Currently, the App Server supports Transport Layer Security (TLS) versions 1.2 and greater.
100	
101	### Environment Variables
102	
103	Code running on the App Server has access to the following environment variables:
104	
105	- `DEPLOY_TARGET`: ID of the environment.
106	- `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`: The domain name set on the environment.
107	- `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID`: ID of the project that the environment belongs to.
108	
109	## Edge Services
110	
111	Supporting the app server are several edge services, including:
112	
113	- A web application firewall (WAF) to protect your environments from attackers
114	- A proxy server to speed up API requests
115	- A content delivery network (CDN) to cache requests and speed up page loading
116	- Edge functions that process requests and handle redirects
117	
118	The proxy server and CDN are covered in detail in our guide to [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.md). The edge function called the request processor is covered in our guide to [Maximizing Your Cache Hit Ratio](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/maximizing-your-cache-hit-ratio.md).

121	
122	## Admin Tools
123	
124	To manage the settings for your organizations, projects, environments, and bundles, we offer two different tools:
125	
126	1. The [Managed Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/), a web-based UI.
127	2. The [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references?meta=managed-runtime-api\:Summary), a REST API that offers the same functionality as the web-based tool and some additional capabilities.
128	
129	Use the Runtime Admin tool for routine tasks, such as deploying a new code bundle to an environment. Use the API whenever you need programmatic control, such as automatically creating an environment as part of a continuous integration script.
130	
131	The admin tools give you a self-serve way to configure many settings, including:
132

134	- Allowed access control headers
135	- Currently deployed bundle
136	- Deployment region
137	- Proxies
138	- Redirects

142	Access to the admin tools is controlled with Account Manager roles and an API key. For continuous integration (CI) and continuous delivery (CD) processes, dedicated bot users with their own API keys are typically provisioned by your organization.

146	## Constraints

159	- Requests with headers that start with `_` are not supported. These requests will be dropped.
160	- HTTP requests originating from Managed Runtime environments don't use fixed IP addresses. To allow list requests from the App Server use the [AWS IP Range](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-ip-ranges.html) for `EC2`. To allow list requests from Proxies, use `CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_FACING`.
161	- The path prefix `/mobify` is reserved for managed endpoints. These endpoints include:
162	  - `/mobify/ping`: Returns an HTTP 200 response code when the environment is operating correctly.
163	  - `/mobify/redirect/$path`: Returns a similar response as [projects_target_redirect_retrieve](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_retrieve).
164	  - `/mobify/proxy/$name`: Returns a response from a [proxy](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.md).
165	- You can bypass the CDN cache using the HTTP request header: `x-mobify-cachebreaker: 1`
166	- Environment IP Allowlists support up to 250 IP addresses. This limit can't be raised.
167	- Environment access control headers support up to 2 headers. Each header:
168	  - Can contain up to 128 characters.
169	  - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and - and \_ characters
170	  - See [Access Control Headers](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#access-control-headers).
171	
172	### Rendering
173	
174	- The execution time for App Server requests is limited to 20 seconds for production environments and 16 seconds for non-production environments. After this time, an HTTP 502 is returned.
175	- Unhandled promise rejections break app rendering.
176	
177	### Deployments
178	
179	- The maximum size for bundles is 400 MB and the maximum size of all `ssr_only` and `ssr_shared` files within the bundle is 249 MB.
180	- Static assets that can be uploaded and served are limited to the following content types: `application/javascript`, `application/json`, `image/png` ,`image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/svg+xml`, `image/webp`, `text/css`, `text/plain` and fonts (`ttf`, `woff`, `woff2`, `otf`, etc). All other content types need to be served by an external system.
181	
182	### Proxies
183	
184	Managed Runtime Proxies have different [constraints](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/proxying-requests.html#constraints).
185	
186	## Availability
187	
188	You can subscribe to updates regarding the availability of Managed Runtime services on [Salesforce Status](https://status.salesforce.com/products/B2C_Commerce_Cloud).
189

# Managed Runtime Overview

[Managed Runtime](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.md) provides the infrastructure to deploy, host, and monitor your PWA Kit storefront.

:::important
Managed Runtime only supports applications created from a PWA Kit template. The source code for the available templates can be found in the `template-*` folders in the [PWA Kit repository](https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/tree/develop/packages) on GitHub.
:::

This guide covers the main parts of Managed Runtime and how to access it.

::include{src="../../shared/managed-runtime-access.md"}

:::important
Before you can use Managed Runtime and Runtime Admin, ask your B2C Commerce administrator to add one of these roles to your account in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.
:::

## Environments

An **environment** is the term used to describe all of the cloud infrastructure and configuration values for a particular storefront hosted by Managed Runtime. Environments are used to separate your production storefront from other storefronts that are deployed for other purposes, such as development or testing.

:::note
In the [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary), environments are called “targets,” but both terms refer to the same thing.
:::

Because environments run on highly efficient microservices that automatically scale up and down, you can create as many environments as you need at no additional cost. For example, you could create a short-lived environment dedicated to a single agile development sprint or for a single user story within that sprint. When you no longer need an environment, we encourage you to delete them.

### Production Environments

Environments marked as production are prioritized for monitoring by Salesforce’s Support team. For production environments, you can also [Debug Using Log Center](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/debugging.html#debug-using-log-center). To mark an environment as a production, you have two choices:

1. Use the Runtime Admin tool. Step-by-step instructions for creating an environment or editing an existing environment are found in the [Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#environments) section of the Administration guide.
2. Use the Managed Runtime API. The [projects_target_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_create) and [projects_target_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_partial_update) endpoints both feature the `is_production` parameter. To mark an environment as production with these endpoints, set `is_production` to `true`.

:::important
By default, you can mark up to 10 environments as production. To increase your limit, contact Support.
:::

## Bundles

The storefront code that runs on an environment is called a **bundle**. Use the developer tools included in PWA Kit to generate a bundle and push it to Managed Runtime.

:::note
A bundle is a snapshot of your code at a specific point in time. It’s *immutable*: After a bundle has been created, it can’t be changed. Having this complete and accurate history of bundles makes troubleshooting deployments easier.
:::

After pushing the bundle, you can use the Runtime Admin or Managed Runtime API to designate that bundle as “deployed.” Each project can have multiple bundles, but each environment can have only one bundle that's designated as deployed. You can change which bundle is designated as deployed at any time. For more information, see [Push and Deploy Bundles](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/pushing-and-deploying-bundles.md).

## Projects and Organizations

To help you manage multiple environments, each environment also belongs to a **project** and each project belongs to an **organization**. An organization can contain multiple projects for multiple storefronts and each project can contain multiple environments. A Managed Runtime user can belong to multiple organizations to separate different work streams.

Each organization can have a maximum of 100 total environments and a maximum of 10 production environments. If you need to raise these limits, contact your Salesforce Support representative.

Organizations and user organization membership is determined by settings in Account Manager. A user can belong to an organization as either a member or an admin. Members can only interact with the projects in Managed Runtime that they’ve been assigned a project role to. Admins can interact with all the projects within an organization.

:::important
To assign a user the admin organization membership, contact Salesforce Support.
:::

## Users, Abilities, and Roles

All users must be assigned the `Managed Runtime User` or `Managed Runtime Admin` via [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com) for accessing Managed Runtime.

### Organization Roles and Permissions

Any user can have the following capabilities for a Managed Runtime organization:

- **Browse:** View all projects for an Organization.
- **Certificate:** View or manage TLS Certificates for an organization.

### Project Roles and Permissions

Any user can have the following capabilities for a Managed Runtime project:

- **Browse:** View the project in Runtime Admin.
- **Manage Redirects:** Manage redirects for the project. Please review the [Redirects documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html?q=Redirects#redirects) to learn more.
- **Deploy:** Deploy new bundles or revert the deployment to an older bundle.
- **Manage Team:** View, add, invite, remove, and edit the roles of team members for the project.
- **Access Logs:** Tail logs across all environments.
- **View and Manage Environment Variables:** See and manage environment variables in each environment. See [Environment Variables](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/environment-variables.md).

Each user is assigned a project role that determines which abilities they have. (A user can only have *one* role.) Project roles can be assigned to any user within an organization.

The following table shows which abilities are associated with each project role:

| Project Role | Browse | Manage Redirects | Deploy | Manage Team | Access Logs | View and Manage Environment Variables |
| :----------- | :----- | :--------------- | :----- | :---------- | :---------- | :------------------------------------ |
| Admin        | Yes    | Yes              | Yes    | Yes         | Yes         | Yes                                   |
| Developer    | Yes    | Yes              | Yes    | No          | Yes         | Yes                                   |
| Marketer     | Yes    | Yes              | No     | No          | No          | No                                    |
| Viewer       | Yes    | No               | No     | No          | No          | No                                    |

## App Server

Within each Managed Runtime environment, the [React](https://reactjs.org/) app in the published bundle runs inside a [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) environment. To respond to page requests and render the results, we use the [Express](https://expressjs.com/) web framework with the help of PWA Kit’s [rendering](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/rendering.md) and [routing](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/routing.md) systems. We call this combination of React, Node, and Express the **App Server**. (Although, technically speaking, the App Server runs on “serverless” technology.) The App Server is optimized to run on cloud infrastructure that offers low computing costs, high availability, fast rendering, and massive scaling capacity.

Because PWA Kit’s rendering and routing system handles the differences between local development environments and Managed Runtime environments, your code runs in a predictable way when you deploy it. This predictability unlocks your development team’s productivity by encouraging them to deploy bundles more frequently.

Currently, the App Server supports Transport Layer Security (TLS) versions 1.2 and greater.

### Environment Variables

Code running on the App Server has access to the following environment variables:

- `DEPLOY_TARGET`: ID of the environment.
- `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`: The domain name set on the environment.
- `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID`: ID of the project that the environment belongs to.

## Edge Services

Supporting the app server are several edge services, including:

- A web application firewall (WAF) to protect your environments from attackers
- A proxy server to speed up API requests
- A content delivery network (CDN) to cache requests and speed up page loading
- Edge functions that process requests and handle redirects

The proxy server and CDN are covered in detail in our guide to [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.md). The edge function called the request processor is covered in our guide to [Maximizing Your Cache Hit Ratio](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/maximizing-your-cache-hit-ratio.md).

Managed Runtime’s edge services are strategically distributed throughout our public cloud infrastructure. Each service is located as close to the user as possible for faster performance.

## Admin Tools

To manage the settings for your organizations, projects, environments, and bundles, we offer two different tools:

1. The [Managed Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/), a web-based UI.
2. The [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references?meta=managed-runtime-api\:Summary), a REST API that offers the same functionality as the web-based tool and some additional capabilities.

Use the Runtime Admin tool for routine tasks, such as deploying a new code bundle to an environment. Use the API whenever you need programmatic control, such as automatically creating an environment as part of a continuous integration script.

The admin tools give you a self-serve way to configure many settings, including:

- Allowed IP addresses
- Allowed access control headers
- Currently deployed bundle
- Deployment region
- Proxies
- Redirects
- User permissions
- Production environment flag

Access to the admin tools is controlled with Account Manager roles and an API key. For continuous integration (CI) and continuous delivery (CD) processes, dedicated bot users with their own API keys are typically provisioned by your organization.

Fun fact: Like your storefront, the Runtime Admin tool is a headless React app that is deployed to Managed Runtime.

## Constraints

While building your storefront, keep the following constraints of Managed Runtime environments in mind:

### Environments

- Environments only respond to requests whose HTTP `Host` header matches their External Hostname set in Runtime Admin.
- A hostname can be set as the External Hostname for only one environment at a time. Setting a hostname that's already in use by another environment fails.
- The path `/` only accepts HTTP GET requests.
- Request and response size can’t exceed 6 MB.
- The maximum size of the HTTP request line and headers is 10240 bytes. Requests exceeding this size return an [HTTP 413 Content Too Large](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/413).
  - Of the 10,240 bytes, 1,500 bytes are reserved for internal use, 1,800 bytes for authorization headers, and 1,000 bytes for Salesforce B2C Commerce API (SCAPI). 5,940 bytes are left for custom request headers, including cookies.
- Cookies, including the HTTP request `Cookie` and HTTP response `Set-Cookie` header aren't supported by default. They can be enabled by setting the `allow_cookies` attribute on an environment with the [projects_target_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_partial_update) endpoint. You can also enable cookies in the [Environment Settings](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#edit-environment-settings) in [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). Cookies are supported in PWA Kit version 3.1.0 or greater. See [Personalize with Cookies](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/personalize-with-cookies.md).
- Requests with headers that start with `_` are not supported. These requests will be dropped.
- HTTP requests originating from Managed Runtime environments don't use fixed IP addresses. To allow list requests from the App Server use the [AWS IP Range](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-ip-ranges.html) for `EC2`. To allow list requests from Proxies, use `CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_FACING`.
- The path prefix `/mobify` is reserved for managed endpoints. These endpoints include:
  - `/mobify/ping`: Returns an HTTP 200 response code when the environment is operating correctly.
  - `/mobify/redirect/$path`: Returns a similar response as [projects_target_redirect_retrieve](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_retrieve).
  - `/mobify/proxy/$name`: Returns a response from a [proxy](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.md).
- You can bypass the CDN cache using the HTTP request header: `x-mobify-cachebreaker: 1`
- Environment IP Allowlists support up to 250 IP addresses. This limit can't be raised.
- Environment access control headers support up to 2 headers. Each header:
  - Can contain up to 128 characters.
  - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and - and \_ characters
  - See [Access Control Headers](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#access-control-headers).

### Rendering

- The execution time for App Server requests is limited to 20 seconds for production environments and 16 seconds for non-production environments. After this time, an HTTP 502 is returned.
- Unhandled promise rejections break app rendering.

### Deployments

- The maximum size for bundles is 400 MB and the maximum size of all `ssr_only` and `ssr_shared` files within the bundle is 249 MB.
- Static assets that can be uploaded and served are limited to the following content types: `application/javascript`, `application/json`, `image/png` ,`image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/svg+xml`, `image/webp`, `text/css`, `text/plain` and fonts (`ttf`, `woff`, `woff2`, `otf`, etc). All other content types need to be served by an external system.

### Proxies

Managed Runtime Proxies have different [constraints](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/proxying-requests.html#constraints).

## Availability

You can subscribe to updates regarding the availability of Managed Runtime services on [Salesforce Status](https://status.salesforce.com/products/B2C_Commerce_Cloud).

## Next Steps

Now that you have an overview of the main parts of Managed Runtime, it’s time to get hands-on! A good place to start is the [Push and Deploy Bundles](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/pushing-and-deploying-bundles.md) guide.

::include{src="../../shared/managed-runtime-access.md"}

:::important
Before you can use Managed Runtime and Runtime Admin, ask your B2C Commerce administrator to add one of these roles to your account in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.
:::

## See Also

- [Managed Runtime Administration](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.md)
- [Managed Runtime API guide](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/using-the-managed-runtime-api.md)
- [Managed Runtime API reference](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary)
- [Video: How to Use the Managed Runtime Admin Tool | Configure PWA Kit](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zxE1SD3FuzM)

1 # Managed Runtime Administration 2 3 Managed Runtime makes it easy to manage your organizations, projects, environments, and bundles associated with your PWA Kit storefront. This guide describes the growing list of administration tasks that are possible in the web-based [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/) tool. All of the administration tasks described in this guide, and many more, can also be done using the [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary). 4 5 :::important 6 Before you continue, make sure that you have access to Managed Runtime and [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). To provision Managed Runtime, contact your Success Manager. For Runtime Admin, contact your B2C Commerce administrator and ask them to add either one of the following roles to your account using Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**. 7 ::: 8 9 ## Organization 10 11 Organization-level administration allows you to manage users and certificates across all projects within your organization. These tasks are typically performed by organization admins or users with specific organizational permissions. 12 13 ### Managing Organization Users 14 15 Organization admins can manage user access and permissions at the organization level, which affects user access across all projects within the organization. 16 17 #### Add Organization Users 18 19 To add a user at the organization level: 20 21 1. Log in to [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com/). 22 2. Find the users in your organization that need access. 23 3. Add the **Managed Runtime Admin** or **Managed Runtime User** role and save. 24 Users should now be able to log into [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/) for your organization. 25 26 :::note 27 Users added at the organization level still need to be assigned specific project roles to access individual projects. 28 ::: 29 30 #### Edit Organization User Permissions 31 32 To modify a user's organization-level permissions: 33 34 1. Navigate to **Organiation Users**. 35 2. Click **Edit** next to the user's name. 36 3. Modify the permissions as needed. 37 - **Certificates**: Allows the user to view, request, manage, and renew TLS certificates. 38 - **View All Projects**: Allows read-only access to all projects within the organization. 39 4. Click **Save**. 40 41 #### Remove Organization Users 42 43 To remove a user from the organization: 44 45 1. Log in to [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com/). 46 2. Find the users in your organization that need access. 47 3. Remove the **Managed Runtime Admin** or **Managed Runtime User** role and save. 48 49 :::warning 50 Removing a user from Managed Runtime revokes their access to all projects within the organization. 51 ::: 52 53 ### Certificate Management 54 55 Organization admins and users with the **Manage Certificates** permission can manage TLS certificates for environments using the Managed Runtime CDN. 56 57 #### Prerequisites for Certificate Management 58 59 - Organization Admin role OR **Manage Certificates** permission. 60 - Access to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). 61 62 #### Request a Certificate 63 64 To request a new TLS certificate: 65 66 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). 67 2. Navigate to **Certificates** for an organization. 68 3. Click **Request Certificate**. 69 4. Enter the domains you want to include in the certificate. 70 - Fully qualified domains (e.g., `www.example.com`, `staging.example.com`) 71 - Wildcard domains (e.g., `*.example.com`) 72 5. Click **Send Request**. 73 74 The certificate request will be processed, and you'll receive domain validation instructions. 75 76 #### Domain Validation 77 78 After requesting a certificate, you must validate domain ownership. 79 80 1. Navigate to **Certificate** and click on the pending certificate. 81 2. Copy the CNAME records provided for domain validation. 82 3. Add these CNAME records to your DNS configuration. 83 4. Validation records must be created within **72 hours** of receiving the validation details. 84 5. After the DNS records are in place, the certificate request will be validated and available to use with any environments within the organization. 85 86 Example validation record: 87 88 ``` 89 _xyz.example.com CNAME _abc.acm-validations.aws 90 ``` 91 92 #### Monitor Certificate Status 93 94 To view the status of your certificates: 95 96 1. Navigate to **Certificates**. 97 2. View the certificate list with validation status indicators. 98 - **In Progress**: Awaiting domain validation. 99 - **Validation Completed**: Certificate is validated and ready for use. 100 - **Failed**: Validation failed because the provided CNAME record wasn't added on time. 101 102 #### Certificate Renewal 103 104 Managed Runtime automatically renews certificates as long as: 105 106 - The domain validation CNAME records remain in place. 107 - The certificate is actively used by at least one environment. 108 109 #### Associate Certificates with Environments 110 111 To use a certificate with an environment: 112 113 1. Go to the project's Overview page. 114 2. Click the environment name. 115 3. Click **Environment Settings**. 116 4. Under **Advanced** settings, click **Edit**. 117 5. Select the appropriate certificate from the **Certificate** dropdown. 118 6. For wildcard certificates, provide a valid subdomain. 119 7. Click **Update**. 120 8. Follow the instructions in [Launching Your Storefront](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/launching-your-storefront.html#6-perform-the-cutover). 121 122 :::important 123 - Users must have the **Project Admin** or **Project Developer** role and the organization **View** or **Manage** certificate permission to change certificates. 124 - Certificates can only be used with environments in the same organization. 125 - Changes to certificate associations require environment redeployment. 126 ::: 127 128 #### Certificate Troubleshooting 129 130 If you encounter issues with certificates: 131 132 - **Domain Validation Fails**: Verify CNAME records are correctly configured and propagated with the validation window. 133 134 ## Projects 135 136 Projects help you manage multiple environments within an organization. Every PWA Kit project needs a corresponding project within Managed Runtime for deploying and hosting the storefront code on Salesforce’s public cloud infrastructure. 137 138 :::note 139 While this guide describes how to manage projects using the web-based Runtime Admin tool, you can use the B2C Commerce CLI to manage Managed Runtime (MRT) projects, environments, and deployments directly from your terminal. First, see [B2C CLI, MCP and Tooling SDK](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/b2c-developer-tooling.md) to install the tool and authenticate. 140 141 Once configured, use the CLI to streamline MRT administration, for example: 142 143 ```bash 144 # List all Managed Runtime projects 145 b2c mrt project list 146 147 # Deploy a specific bundle to an environment 148 b2c mrt bundle deploy --project --environment 149 150 # Manage environments and environment variables 151 b2c mrt env list --project 152 b2c mrt env var --project --environment 153 154 # Manage URL redirects for an environment 155 b2c mrt env redirect --project --environment 156 ``` 157 158 For a complete list of Managed Runtime CLI commands, see [MRT Commands](https://salesforcecommercecloud.github.io/b2c-developer-tooling/cli/mrt.html). 159 ::: 160 161 ### Create a Project 162 163 To create a project in Runtime Admin: 164 165 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com). 166 2. Click **New Project**. 167 3. Under **Add New Project Details**, enter a name for the project. 168 4. Under **Set Environment Defaults**, review the default settings that apply to new environments in the project. Server-Side Cookie Access is enabled by default for new projects, which lets your storefront access and manage cookies from server-side code. To turn it off, clear the setting. 169 5. Click **Create Project**. 170 171 :::note 172 When you first create a project, your site isn’t accessible on the web until after the necessary cloud infrastructure is deployed. This deployment process can take up to 40 minutes. 173 ::: 174 175 ### Find a Project in Runtime Admin 176 177 The instructions for the rest of the administration tasks in this guide all assume that you’re starting from a project Overview page in Runtime Admin. 178 179 To find an existing project and open its Overview page: 180 181 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). 182 2. Select an organization from the organization menu (top left), if necessary. 183 3. Click the name of the project. (To see the project, you must be assigned one of the project roles described previously.) 184 185 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-1.png) 186 187 To find a project quickly, use the project search box to filter across all the projects in your organization, not just the ones on the current page. You can also choose how many projects to show per page (20, 50, or 100). Your search term and page size are saved in the page URL, so you can bookmark or share a filtered view. 188 189 To quickly switch between projects, use the project menu at the top of the page. 190 191 ### View and Edit Project Settings 192 193 The Project Settings page is where you can do the following tasks: 194 195 - Look up the project ID and ensure that it matches a PWA Kit configuration. 196 - Edit the project ID. 197 - View and edit the project’s name and URL. 198 - Set environment defaults, including the default server architecture and proxy user agent for new environments. 199 - Delete the project. 200 - Manage deployment notifications. (See next section.) 201 202 To access the Project Settings page: 203 204 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 205 2. Click Project Settings from the left navigation. 206 207 To edit the settings, click **Edit**, make your edits, and click **Update**. To discard your edits, click **Cancel**. 208 209 To delete a project, click **Delete**, enter the project name to confirm, and click **Yes, Delete**. To keep the project, click **No, Keep**. 210 211 ## Deployment Notifications 212 213 You can choose to be notified by email whenever any of the following deployment events happen: 214 215 - Start Deployment 216 - Successful Deployment 217 - Failed Deployment 218 219 ### Add a Notification 220 221 To add a notification: 222 223 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 224 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 225 3. Click **Add Notification**. 226 4. Select one or more environments to be notified about. 227 5. Select one or more deployment events. 228 6. Enter email addresses for all notification recipients. 229 7. Click **Add Notification**. 230 231 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-5.png) 232 233 ### Edit a Notification 234 235 To edit a notification: 236 237 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 238 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 239 3. Click the **...** button next to the notification. 240 4. Click **Edit**. 241 5. Change any of the notification settings. 242 6. Click **Update Notification**. 243 244 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-6.png) 245 246 ### Remove a Notification 247 248 To remove a notification: 249 250 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 251 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 252 3. Click the **...** button next to the notification. 253 4. Click **Remove**. 254 5. Click **Yes, Remove**. 255 256 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-7.png) 257 258 ## Environments 259 260 Environments are used to separate your production storefront from other storefronts that are deployed for other purposes, such as development or testing. To learn more about environments and other related concepts, see the [Managed Runtime Overview](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/mrt-overview.md). 261 262 ### Create an Environment 263 264 To create an environment in Runtime Admin: 265 266 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 267 268 2. Click **New Environment** 269 270 3. Enter a name for the environment. 271 272 4. Select a [region](#supported-regions) for deploying to Salesforce’s public cloud infrastructure. 273 274 5. If the environment is a production environment: 275 276 - Mark it as production. If you have reached your limit of production environments, contact Support. For more information, see [Production Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/mrt-overview.html#production-environments). 277 - Add one or more site IDs to associate with the environment. 278 279 6. Select a B2C Commerce instance to connect to the environment. 280 281 7. Click **Complete Setup**. 282 283 :::note 284 - The default region for new environments is US East (N. Virginia) because it’s located closest to on-demand sandboxes, which are commonly associated with development and testing environments. 285 - If you previously created an environment, you can [Edit Environment Settings](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html?#edit-environment-settings) to connect it to a B2C Commerce instance and one or more site IDs. 286 - There is no difference in the resources provided to a production or non-production environment. All environments automatically scale to handle traffic in the same way. For details, see [Production Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/mrt-overview.html#production-environments). 287 ::: 288 289 ### Supported Regions 290 291 All supported regions have a paired backup region for failovers. You're responsible for ensuring that your application runs correctly in the selected primary and backup regions: 292 293 294 295 296 297 298 299 300 301 302 303 304 305 306 307 308 309 310 311 312 313 314 315 316 317 318 319 320 321 322 323 324 325 326 327 328 329 330 331 332 333 334 335 336 337 338 339 340 341 342 343 344 345 346 347 348 349 350 351 352 353 354 355 356 357 358 359 360 361 362 363 364 365 366 367 368 369 370 371 372 373 374 375 376 377 378 379 380 381 382 383 384 385 386 387 388 389 390
