391 392 ### Deploy a Bundle 393 394 For any site that uses PWA Kit and Managed Runtime, you can only designate **one bundle at a time** as deployed for each environment. 395 396 1. Go to a project’s overview page. 397 2. Click the name of the environment you want to deploy to. For example: **production**. 398 3. Under the heading **Bundles**, click the **Deploy** button next to the bundle you want to deploy. 399 4. Click **Confirm Deploy**. 400 5. Wait until the deployment is complete. 401 402 When the deployment has successfully completed, the bundle appears underneath the heading **Deployed Bundle**. (For your first deployment to a new environment, the process can take up to an hour to complete.) 403 404 ### Delete a Bundle 405 406 For any site that uses PWA Kit and Managed Runtime, you can delete only non-deployed bundles form a project. 407 408 1. In the project’s overview page, click an environment. 409 2. Select one or more bundles that aren't currently deployed. 410 3. Click **Delete**. 411 4. When asked to confirm, click **Delete**. 412 5. Wait until the deletion is completed. 413 414 Deletions are handled asynchronously and can take time to process. 415 416 ### Edit Environment Settings 417 418 The Environment Settings page is where you can do many administration tasks in one place, including: 419 420 - Rename an environment or environment ID. 421 - Change the deployment region. 422 - Enable or disable server-side cookies. New projects have Server-Side Cookie Access enabled by default. Existing projects continue to have server-side cookies turned off by default. See [Personalize with Cookies](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/personalize-with-cookies.md). 423 - Enable or disable [Source Maps](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/debugging.html#source-maps). 424 - Allow traffic with specific IP addresses or a trusted access control header to access an environment. See [Access Control Headers](#access-control-headers). 425 - Configure proxies for an environment. See [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.md) for more information. 426 - Control whether proxied requests forward the shopper's original user agent or replace it with the Amazon CloudFront infrastructure user agent. See [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html#request-modifications). 427 - Mark an environment as production. 428 - Add, edit, or remove site IDs associated with an environment. 429 - Add or edit an environment’s connection to a B2C Commerce instance. 430 - Delete an environment. 431 432 To access the Environment Settings page: 433 434 1. Go to a project’s Overview page 435 2. Click the name of the environment whose settings you want to edit. 436 3. Click **Environment Settings** from the left navigation. 437 438 To make edits, click the **Edit** button next to either the **General** settings or the **Advanced** settings. After making your edits, click **Update** to save your changes or click **Cancel** to discard your changes. 439 440 ### Server-Side Rendering Architecture 441 442 Managed Runtime supports two processor architectures for Server-Side Rendering (SSR): ARM and x86. The architecture determines the underlying compute infrastructure used to render your storefront. 443 444 #### ARM Architecture (Default for New Projects) 445 446 ARM architecture is the default for all new projects created in Managed Runtime. ARM processors offer several advantages. 447 448 - **Enhanced Performance**: ARM architecture provides efficient processing capabilities optimized for modern web workloads. 449 - **Modern Infrastructure**: Built on the latest cloud computing technologies. 450 451 **Who Can Use It**: All new Managed Runtime projects automatically use ARM architecture. 452 453 #### x86 Architecture (Scheduled for Retirement) 454 455 :::warning 456 The x86 architecture is retiring on **January 31, 2027**. After that date, environments running on x86 can't be deployed. Environments aren't deleted and continue to respond to requests. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. 457 ::: 458 459 The x86 architecture is available for existing customers until its retirement on January 31, 2027. 460 461 **Who**: Existing customers with projects created before ARM architecture was introduced can continue using x86 until January 31, 2027. 462 463 #### Choosing an Architecture 464 465 - **New Projects**: ARM architecture is automatically selected and is the recommended choice for all new projects. 466 - **Existing projects**: x86 architecture is retiring on January 31, 2027. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. Admins can switch existing environments to ARM at any time in Runtime Admin under environment settings. Most projects require no code changes. If your project uses architecture-specific native modules, test in a non-production environment before switching production. 467 468 #### Project-Level Default Architecture 469 470 You can set a default architecture at the project level that automatically applies to all new environments created within that project. This setting streamlines environment creation by eliminating the need to select an architecture for each new environment. 471 472 How to Set Project-Level Default: 473 474 1. Go to a project's Overview page. 475 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 476 3. Under **Environment Defaults** and **Server Architecture**, select either **ARM** or **x86**. 477 4. Click **Update**. 478 479 All new environments created in the project automatically use the selected default architecture. Existing environments aren't affected by changes to the project-level default. 480 481 ### Clear an Environment's CDN Cache 482 483 You can clear some or all of an environment's cached content in the content delivery network (CDN). Clearing the CDN cache helps to ensure that shoppers see the most recent and accurate version of content on your site. 484 485 Use the [projects_target_invalidation_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_invalidation_create) API to clear all cached content, specific URLs, or directories. 486 487 It's not possible to clear the CDN cache in Runtime Admin. However, when you redeploy a bundle, that clears all cached content for the associated environment. 488 489 :::note 490 Invalidation of the CDN cache temporarily results in slower performance for the first shoppers accessing the site after the invalidation. 491 ::: 492 493 ## Environment Variables 494 495 See [Environment Variables](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/environment-variables.md). 496 497 ## Access Control Headers 498 499 Access control headers allow you to restrict access to an environment so that only trusted traffic coming from your content delivery network (CDN) or development team is allowed. Restricting access is important to ensure that bots don't go around your CDN perimeter security settings and to ensure that search crawlers don’t index content from the wrong domain or environment. 500 501 If Allowed IP addresses are also set, requests with either a valid IP address or an access control header are allowed through. 502 503 ### Usage 504 505 Set access control headers by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 506 507 Incoming requests are allowed only if an `x-sfdc-access-control` request header is present with a valid value. 508 509 ### Constraints 510 511 A header value is made up of your chosen set of characters. Each header value: 512 513 - Must be at least 9 characters long 514 - Can contain up to 128 characters 515 - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and `-` and `_` characters 516 517 Access control headers are not available to code running in a Managed Runtime environment. 518 519 ### Rotate Access Control Headers 520 521 You’re responsible for ensuring that the access control header value is securely stored and shared only with trusted individuals. We strongly recommend rotating the access control header on a regular basis. 522 523 To rotate an access control header: 524 525 - Add an access control header value to the Managed Runtime environment by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 526 - Wait for the Environment redeploy to complete successfully. Verify requests to the environment with the new header value succeed with a command such as: 527 528 ```bash 529 curl https://myproject-mytarget.mobify-storefront.com/ -H "x-sfdc-access-control: 123456789" -o /dev/null 530 ``` 531 532 - Update your CDN or browser to send the `x-sfdc-access-control` request header with the updated value. 533 - Test that traffic is being allowed through as expected. 534 - Remove the original access control header value by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 535 536 **See Also** 537 538 - [Configure Your Environment](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/launching-your-storefront.html#5-configure-your-environment) 539 540 ## Redirects 541 542 A redirect allows you to forward a request from the requested URL to a different URL. Redirects can help avoid disruptions to the user experience caused by changes to your storefront. For example, consider a seasonal campaign page for spring. When the spring campaign ends and is replaced with a summer campaign, you can redirect from the spring URL to the summer URL. 543 544 Redirects is a powerful feature that can have significant security consequences on your storefront, including redirecting to malicious URLs or assets. Please be careful when assigning roles to your users that give them Redirect access. 545 546 ### Create a Redirect 547 548 :::tip 549 Before creating a redirect in a production environment, we recommend that you create it in a staging environment first. 550 ::: 551 552 You can also create one or more redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_create](/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_create) API endpoint. 553 554 To create a redirect using Runtime Admin: 555 556 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 557 2. Click the name of the environment where you want to create the redirect. 558 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 559 4. Click **Create Redirect**. 560 5. In the **Redirect From** field, enter a relative URL path. For example, to redirect visitors from the URL `www.example.com/winter`, enter `/winter`. 561 6. In the **Redirect To** field, enter a relative URL path. 562 7. If needed, enable forwarding of query parameters and the wildcard path. (More information on forwarding settings in a moment.) 563 8. From the **Redirect Type** dropdown menu, select a redirect type based on the HTTP status code. (More information on status codes in a moment.) 564 9. Click **Create Redirect**. 565 566 Let’s look at the options for creating a redirect in more detail. 567 568 #### Paths 569 570 The value that you enter in the **Redirect From** field must always be a *relative* path. The **Redirect To** field can be either a relative path or a full URL. For example, imagine that we want to redirect visitors from `www.example.com/spring` to `www.example.com/summer`. The **Redirect From** field must be `/spring`. The **Redirect To** field can be either `/summer` or `www.example.com/summer`. 571 572 #### Wildcards 573 574 You can add an asterisk character (`*`) to the end of the **Redirect From** URL to indicate a wildcard. A wildcard matches any (0 or more) characters in the URL. For example, a redirect from `/a/*` would match `/a/`, `/a/b`, and `/a/b/c`. 575 576 A wildcard character can only be used at the end of the **Redirect From** URL. 577 578 Standard redirects are processed first by Managed Runtime, followed by redirects with wildcards. 579 580 #### HTTP Status Codes 581 582 Most redirects use the Permanent 301 status code, but you can also select Temporary 302. If you’re unsure which HTTP status code to use, consult this [status code explainer](https://moz.com/learn/seo/redirection) from MOZ.com. 583 584 #### Forwarding Query Parameters 585 586 Some requests contain query string parameters that you also want to include in the redirected request. For example, the relative path `/spring-landing-page` can be appended with a query string for analytics tracking, such as `/spring-landing-page?gclid=123`. 587 588 To enable query parameter forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Query Parameters**. Otherwise, query string parameters from the source URL aren’t included in the redirect URL. 589 590 What happens when both the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** URLs both have query strings and forwarding is enabled? In this case, the redirect URL includes a combination of the two query strings. The query parameters from the **Redirect To** URL are appended to the query string in the request. For example, imagine your application receives a request for the relative path `/spring?year=2019`. If you’ve chosen to redirect `/spring` to `/summer?year=2020`, the redirect URL is `/summer?year=2019&year=2020` when forwarding is enabled. 591 592 #### Forwarding Wildcard Path 593 594 You can automatically include any path that comes after the wildcard portion of the **Redirect From** URL in the **Redirect To** URL. For example: if `/a/*` matches `/a/b/c` in the **Redirect From** URL, and the **Redirect To** URL is `/z/`, the redirect URL is `/z/b/c`. 595 596 To enable wildcard path forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Wildcard Path**. 597 598 ### Clone Redirects 599 600 :::tip 601 We recommend that you always create redirects in a staging environment and clone them into production after testing them. 602 ::: 603 604 You can copy all the redirects from one environment to another using the clone redirects feature. 605 606 You can also clone redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_clone_create ](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_clone_create) API endpoint. 607 608 To clone redirects using Runtime Admin: 609 610 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 611 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirects that you want to clone. 612 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 613 4. Click **Clone Redirects**. The **Clone Redirects** form appears. The current environment is listed under **From Environment** (the source). 614 5. Under **To Environment**, select the environment that you want to clone the redirects into (the destination). 615 6. Click **Clone n Redirects**. (Where n is the number of redirects to be cloned.) 616 617 :::warning 618 When you clone redirects, you’re replacing *all* the redirects in the destination environment with *all* the redirects from the source environment. 619 ::: 620 621 ### Edit a Redirect 622 623 You can also edit a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_partial_update) API endpoint. 624 625 To edit the settings for an existing redirect using Runtime Admin: 626 627 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 628 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to edit. 629 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 630 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 631 5. Click **Edit**. 632 6. Update the settings. 633 7. Click **Update Redirect**. 634 635 ### Delete a Redirect 636 637 You can also delete a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_destroy](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_destroy) API endpoint. 638 639 To delete a redirect using Runtime Admin: 640 641 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 642 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to delete. 643 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 644 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 645 5. Click **Delete**. 646 6. Click **Yes, Delete Redirect**. 647 648 ### Troubleshooting Redirects 649 650 If a redirect isn’t working as expected, try these troubleshooting steps: 651 652 - [Clear your browser cache](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop\&hl=en) because redirects are cached. 653 - Verify that you’re viewing the settings for the correct environment. 654 - Edit the redirect and verify that the correct values are entered in the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** fields. 655 656 ### Technical Limitations with Redirects 657 658 Redirects have the following technical limitations: 659 660 - Each environment can have a maximum of 10,000 redirects. 661 - Each environment has its own set of redirects. It is your responsibility to keep them in sync using cloning. 662 - The redirects feature supports simple redirects from one path to another. For complex redirects with conditionals use Express.js' [redirects support](http://expressjs.com/en/api.html#res.redirect) in `ssr.js`. 663 - Redirects created with the Runtime Admin tool or the Managed Runtime API are not run on local development environments. 664 - Redirects are not triggered by page transitions in the PWA Kit application; they can only be triggered by an HTTP request. 665 - To load a redirect in the context of a storefront, use the managed endpoint `/mobify/redirect/$path`. 666 667 ## Users 668 669 Here’s how to manage your users. 670 671 ### Add a User 672 673 To add a user to a project: 674 675 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 676 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 677 3. Click **New User**. 678 4. Enter the user’s email address. (Make sure that the user is part of your organization and has either one of the following roles in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.) 679 5. Select a role. 680 6. Click **Add User**. 681 682 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-2.png) 683 684 ### Change a User’s Role 685 686 To change a user’s role: 687 688 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 689 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 690 3. Click the **...** button next to the user’s name. 691 4. Click **Edit**. 692 5. Select a role. 693 6. Click the popup menu that appears. 694 7. Select a new role. 695 8. Click **Save**. 696 697 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-3.png) 698 699 For a list of user abilities associated with each role, see the [Managed Runtime Overview](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/mrt-overview.md). 700 701 ### Remove a User 702 703 To remove a user from a project: 704 705 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 706 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 707 3. Click the **...** button next to the user’s name. 708 4. Click **Remove**. 709 5. Click **Yes, Remove User**. 710 711 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-4.png) 712

# Managed Runtime Administration Managed Runtime makes it easy to manage your organizations, projects, environments, and bundles associated with your PWA Kit storefront. This guide describes the growing list of administration tasks that are possible in the web-based [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/) tool. All of the administration tasks described in this guide, and many more, can also be done using the [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary). :::important Before you continue, make sure that you have access to Managed Runtime and [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). To provision Managed Runtime, contact your Success Manager. For Runtime Admin, contact your B2C Commerce administrator and ask them to add either one of the following roles to your account using Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**. ::: ## Organization Organization-level administration allows you to manage users and certificates across all projects within your organization. These tasks are typically performed by organization admins or users with specific organizational permissions. ### Managing Organization Users Organization admins can manage user access and permissions at the organization level, which affects user access across all projects within the organization. #### Add Organization Users To add a user at the organization level: 1. Log in to [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com/). 2. Find the users in your organization that need access. 3. Add the **Managed Runtime Admin** or **Managed Runtime User** role and save. Users should now be able to log into [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/) for your organization. :::note Users added at the organization level still need to be assigned specific project roles to access individual projects. ::: #### Edit Organization User Permissions To modify a user's organization-level permissions: 1. Navigate to **Organiation Users**. 2. Click **Edit** next to the user's name. 3. Modify the permissions as needed. - **Certificates**: Allows the user to view, request, manage, and renew TLS certificates. - **View All Projects**: Allows read-only access to all projects within the organization. 4. Click **Save**. #### Remove Organization Users To remove a user from the organization: 1. Log in to [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com/). 2. Find the users in your organization that need access. 3. Remove the **Managed Runtime Admin** or **Managed Runtime User** role and save. :::warning Removing a user from Managed Runtime revokes their access to all projects within the organization. ::: ### Certificate Management Organization admins and users with the **Manage Certificates** permission can manage TLS certificates for environments using the Managed Runtime CDN. #### Prerequisites for Certificate Management - Organization Admin role OR **Manage Certificates** permission. - Access to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). #### Request a Certificate To request a new TLS certificate: 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). 2. Navigate to **Certificates** for an organization. 3. Click **Request Certificate**. 4. Enter the domains you want to include in the certificate. - Fully qualified domains (e.g., `www.example.com`, `staging.example.com`) - Wildcard domains (e.g., `*.example.com`) 5. Click **Send Request**. The certificate request will be processed, and you'll receive domain validation instructions. #### Domain Validation After requesting a certificate, you must validate domain ownership. 1. Navigate to **Certificate** and click on the pending certificate. 2. Copy the CNAME records provided for domain validation. 3. Add these CNAME records to your DNS configuration. 4. Validation records must be created within **72 hours** of receiving the validation details. 5. After the DNS records are in place, the certificate request will be validated and available to use with any environments within the organization. Example validation record: ``` _xyz.example.com CNAME _abc.acm-validations.aws ``` #### Monitor Certificate Status To view the status of your certificates: 1. Navigate to **Certificates**. 2. View the certificate list with validation status indicators. - **In Progress**: Awaiting domain validation. - **Validation Completed**: Certificate is validated and ready for use. - **Failed**: Validation failed because the provided CNAME record wasn't added on time. #### Certificate Renewal Managed Runtime automatically renews certificates as long as: - The domain validation CNAME records remain in place. - The certificate is actively used by at least one environment. #### Associate Certificates with Environments To use a certificate with an environment: 1. Go to the project's Overview page. 2. Click the environment name. 3. Click **Environment Settings**. 4. Under **Advanced** settings, click **Edit**. 5. Select the appropriate certificate from the **Certificate** dropdown. 6. For wildcard certificates, provide a valid subdomain. 7. Click **Update**. 8. Follow the instructions in [Launching Your Storefront](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/launching-your-storefront.html#6-perform-the-cutover). :::important - Users must have the **Project Admin** or **Project Developer** role and the organization **View** or **Manage** certificate permission to change certificates. - Certificates can only be used with environments in the same organization. - Changes to certificate associations require environment redeployment. ::: #### Certificate Troubleshooting If you encounter issues with certificates: - **Domain Validation Fails**: Verify CNAME records are correctly configured and propagated with the validation window. ## Projects Projects help you manage multiple environments within an organization. Every PWA Kit project needs a corresponding project within Managed Runtime for deploying and hosting the storefront code on Salesforce’s public cloud infrastructure. :::note While this guide describes how to manage projects using the web-based Runtime Admin tool, you can use the B2C Commerce CLI to manage Managed Runtime (MRT) projects, environments, and deployments directly from your terminal. First, see [B2C CLI, MCP and Tooling SDK](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/b2c-developer-tooling.md) to install the tool and authenticate. Once configured, use the CLI to streamline MRT administration, for example: ```bash # List all Managed Runtime projects b2c mrt project list # Deploy a specific bundle to an environment b2c mrt bundle deploy --project --environment # Manage environments and environment variables b2c mrt env list --project b2c mrt env var --project --environment # Manage URL redirects for an environment b2c mrt env redirect --project --environment ``` For a complete list of Managed Runtime CLI commands, see [MRT Commands](https://salesforcecommercecloud.github.io/b2c-developer-tooling/cli/mrt.html). ::: ### Create a Project To create a project in Runtime Admin: 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com). 2. Click **New Project**. 3. Under **Add New Project Details**, enter a name for the project. 4. Under **Set Environment Defaults**, review the default settings that apply to new environments in the project. Server-Side Cookie Access is enabled by default for new projects, which lets your storefront access and manage cookies from server-side code. To turn it off, clear the setting. 5. Click **Create Project**. :::note When you first create a project, your site isn’t accessible on the web until after the necessary cloud infrastructure is deployed. This deployment process can take up to 40 minutes. ::: ### Find a Project in Runtime Admin The instructions for the rest of the administration tasks in this guide all assume that you’re starting from a project Overview page in Runtime Admin. To find an existing project and open its Overview page: 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). 2. Select an organization from the organization menu (top left), if necessary. 3. Click the name of the project. (To see the project, you must be assigned one of the project roles described previously.) ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-1.png) To find a project quickly, use the project search box to filter across all the projects in your organization, not just the ones on the current page. You can also choose how many projects to show per page (20, 50, or 100). Your search term and page size are saved in the page URL, so you can bookmark or share a filtered view. To quickly switch between projects, use the project menu at the top of the page. ### View and Edit Project Settings The Project Settings page is where you can do the following tasks: - Look up the project ID and ensure that it matches a PWA Kit configuration. - Edit the project ID. - View and edit the project’s name and URL. - Set environment defaults, including the default server architecture and proxy user agent for new environments. - Delete the project. - Manage deployment notifications. (See next section.) To access the Project Settings page: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click Project Settings from the left navigation. To edit the settings, click **Edit**, make your edits, and click **Update**. To discard your edits, click **Cancel**. To delete a project, click **Delete**, enter the project name to confirm, and click **Yes, Delete**. To keep the project, click **No, Keep**. ## Deployment Notifications You can choose to be notified by email whenever any of the following deployment events happen: - Start Deployment - Successful Deployment - Failed Deployment ### Add a Notification To add a notification: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 3. Click **Add Notification**. 4. Select one or more environments to be notified about. 5. Select one or more deployment events. 6. Enter email addresses for all notification recipients. 7. Click **Add Notification**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-5.png) ### Edit a Notification To edit a notification: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 3. Click the **...** button next to the notification. 4. Click **Edit**. 5. Change any of the notification settings. 6. Click **Update Notification**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-6.png) ### Remove a Notification To remove a notification: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 3. Click the **...** button next to the notification. 4. Click **Remove**. 5. Click **Yes, Remove**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-7.png) ## Environments Environments are used to separate your production storefront from other storefronts that are deployed for other purposes, such as development or testing. To learn more about environments and other related concepts, see the [Managed Runtime Overview](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/mrt-overview.md). ### Create an Environment To create an environment in Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **New Environment** 3. Enter a name for the environment. 4. Select a [region](#supported-regions) for deploying to Salesforce’s public cloud infrastructure. 5. If the environment is a production environment: - Mark it as production. If you have reached your limit of production environments, contact Support. For more information, see [Production Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/mrt-overview.html#production-environments). - Add one or more site IDs to associate with the environment. 6. Select a B2C Commerce instance to connect to the environment. 7. Click **Complete Setup**. :::note - The default region for new environments is US East (N. Virginia) because it’s located closest to on-demand sandboxes, which are commonly associated with development and testing environments. - If you previously created an environment, you can [Edit Environment Settings](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html?#edit-environment-settings) to connect it to a B2C Commerce instance and one or more site IDs. - There is no difference in the resources provided to a production or non-production environment. All environments automatically scale to handle traffic in the same way. For details, see [Production Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/mrt-overview.html#production-environments). ::: ### Supported Regions All supported regions have a paired backup region for failovers. You're responsible for ensuring that your application runs correctly in the selected primary and backup regions:

### Deploy a Bundle For any site that uses PWA Kit and Managed Runtime, you can only designate **one bundle at a time** as deployed for each environment. 1. Go to a project’s overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment you want to deploy to. For example: **production**. 3. Under the heading **Bundles**, click the **Deploy** button next to the bundle you want to deploy. 4. Click **Confirm Deploy**. 5. Wait until the deployment is complete. When the deployment has successfully completed, the bundle appears underneath the heading **Deployed Bundle**. (For your first deployment to a new environment, the process can take up to an hour to complete.) ### Delete a Bundle For any site that uses PWA Kit and Managed Runtime, you can delete only non-deployed bundles form a project. 1. In the project’s overview page, click an environment. 2. Select one or more bundles that aren't currently deployed. 3. Click **Delete**. 4. When asked to confirm, click **Delete**. 5. Wait until the deletion is completed. Deletions are handled asynchronously and can take time to process. ### Edit Environment Settings The Environment Settings page is where you can do many administration tasks in one place, including: - Rename an environment or environment ID. - Change the deployment region. - Enable or disable server-side cookies. New projects have Server-Side Cookie Access enabled by default. Existing projects continue to have server-side cookies turned off by default. See [Personalize with Cookies](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/personalize-with-cookies.md). - Enable or disable [Source Maps](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/debugging.html#source-maps). - Allow traffic with specific IP addresses or a trusted access control header to access an environment. See [Access Control Headers](#access-control-headers). - Configure proxies for an environment. See [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.md) for more information. - Control whether proxied requests forward the shopper's original user agent or replace it with the Amazon CloudFront infrastructure user agent. See [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html#request-modifications). - Mark an environment as production. - Add, edit, or remove site IDs associated with an environment. - Add or edit an environment’s connection to a B2C Commerce instance. - Delete an environment. To access the Environment Settings page: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page 2. Click the name of the environment whose settings you want to edit. 3. Click **Environment Settings** from the left navigation. To make edits, click the **Edit** button next to either the **General** settings or the **Advanced** settings. After making your edits, click **Update** to save your changes or click **Cancel** to discard your changes. ### Server-Side Rendering Architecture Managed Runtime supports two processor architectures for Server-Side Rendering (SSR): ARM and x86. The architecture determines the underlying compute infrastructure used to render your storefront. #### ARM Architecture (Default for New Projects) ARM architecture is the default for all new projects created in Managed Runtime. ARM processors offer several advantages. - **Enhanced Performance**: ARM architecture provides efficient processing capabilities optimized for modern web workloads. - **Modern Infrastructure**: Built on the latest cloud computing technologies. **Who Can Use It**: All new Managed Runtime projects automatically use ARM architecture. #### x86 Architecture (Scheduled for Retirement) :::warning The x86 architecture is retiring on **January 31, 2027**. After that date, environments running on x86 can't be deployed. Environments aren't deleted and continue to respond to requests. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. ::: The x86 architecture is available for existing customers until its retirement on January 31, 2027. **Who**: Existing customers with projects created before ARM architecture was introduced can continue using x86 until January 31, 2027. #### Choosing an Architecture - **New Projects**: ARM architecture is automatically selected and is the recommended choice for all new projects. - **Existing projects**: x86 architecture is retiring on January 31, 2027. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. Admins can switch existing environments to ARM at any time in Runtime Admin under environment settings. Most projects require no code changes. If your project uses architecture-specific native modules, test in a non-production environment before switching production. #### Project-Level Default Architecture You can set a default architecture at the project level that automatically applies to all new environments created within that project. This setting streamlines environment creation by eliminating the need to select an architecture for each new environment. How to Set Project-Level Default: 1. Go to a project's Overview page. 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 3. Under **Environment Defaults** and **Server Architecture**, select either **ARM** or **x86**. 4. Click **Update**. All new environments created in the project automatically use the selected default architecture. Existing environments aren't affected by changes to the project-level default. ### Clear an Environment's CDN Cache You can clear some or all of an environment's cached content in the content delivery network (CDN). Clearing the CDN cache helps to ensure that shoppers see the most recent and accurate version of content on your site. Use the [projects_target_invalidation_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_invalidation_create) API to clear all cached content, specific URLs, or directories. It's not possible to clear the CDN cache in Runtime Admin. However, when you redeploy a bundle, that clears all cached content for the associated environment. :::note Invalidation of the CDN cache temporarily results in slower performance for the first shoppers accessing the site after the invalidation. ::: ## Environment Variables See [Environment Variables](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/environment-variables.md). ## Access Control Headers Access control headers allow you to restrict access to an environment so that only trusted traffic coming from your content delivery network (CDN) or development team is allowed. Restricting access is important to ensure that bots don't go around your CDN perimeter security settings and to ensure that search crawlers don’t index content from the wrong domain or environment. If Allowed IP addresses are also set, requests with either a valid IP address or an access control header are allowed through. ### Usage Set access control headers by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. Incoming requests are allowed only if an `x-sfdc-access-control` request header is present with a valid value. ### Constraints A header value is made up of your chosen set of characters. Each header value: - Must be at least 9 characters long - Can contain up to 128 characters - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and `-` and `_` characters Access control headers are not available to code running in a Managed Runtime environment. ### Rotate Access Control Headers You’re responsible for ensuring that the access control header value is securely stored and shared only with trusted individuals. We strongly recommend rotating the access control header on a regular basis. To rotate an access control header: - Add an access control header value to the Managed Runtime environment by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. - Wait for the Environment redeploy to complete successfully. Verify requests to the environment with the new header value succeed with a command such as: ```bash curl https://myproject-mytarget.mobify-storefront.com/ -H "x-sfdc-access-control: 123456789" -o /dev/null ``` - Update your CDN or browser to send the `x-sfdc-access-control` request header with the updated value. - Test that traffic is being allowed through as expected. - Remove the original access control header value by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. **See Also** - [Configure Your Environment](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/launching-your-storefront.html#5-configure-your-environment) ## Redirects A redirect allows you to forward a request from the requested URL to a different URL. Redirects can help avoid disruptions to the user experience caused by changes to your storefront. For example, consider a seasonal campaign page for spring. When the spring campaign ends and is replaced with a summer campaign, you can redirect from the spring URL to the summer URL. Redirects is a powerful feature that can have significant security consequences on your storefront, including redirecting to malicious URLs or assets. Please be careful when assigning roles to your users that give them Redirect access. ### Create a Redirect :::tip Before creating a redirect in a production environment, we recommend that you create it in a staging environment first. ::: You can also create one or more redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_create](/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_create) API endpoint. To create a redirect using Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment where you want to create the redirect. 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 4. Click **Create Redirect**. 5. In the **Redirect From** field, enter a relative URL path. For example, to redirect visitors from the URL `www.example.com/winter`, enter `/winter`. 6. In the **Redirect To** field, enter a relative URL path. 7. If needed, enable forwarding of query parameters and the wildcard path. (More information on forwarding settings in a moment.) 8. From the **Redirect Type** dropdown menu, select a redirect type based on the HTTP status code. (More information on status codes in a moment.) 9. Click **Create Redirect**. Let’s look at the options for creating a redirect in more detail. #### Paths The value that you enter in the **Redirect From** field must always be a *relative* path. The **Redirect To** field can be either a relative path or a full URL. For example, imagine that we want to redirect visitors from `www.example.com/spring` to `www.example.com/summer`. The **Redirect From** field must be `/spring`. The **Redirect To** field can be either `/summer` or `www.example.com/summer`. #### Wildcards You can add an asterisk character (`*`) to the end of the **Redirect From** URL to indicate a wildcard. A wildcard matches any (0 or more) characters in the URL. For example, a redirect from `/a/*` would match `/a/`, `/a/b`, and `/a/b/c`. A wildcard character can only be used at the end of the **Redirect From** URL. Standard redirects are processed first by Managed Runtime, followed by redirects with wildcards. #### HTTP Status Codes Most redirects use the Permanent 301 status code, but you can also select Temporary 302. If you’re unsure which HTTP status code to use, consult this [status code explainer](https://moz.com/learn/seo/redirection) from MOZ.com. #### Forwarding Query Parameters Some requests contain query string parameters that you also want to include in the redirected request. For example, the relative path `/spring-landing-page` can be appended with a query string for analytics tracking, such as `/spring-landing-page?gclid=123`. To enable query parameter forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Query Parameters**. Otherwise, query string parameters from the source URL aren’t included in the redirect URL. What happens when both the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** URLs both have query strings and forwarding is enabled? In this case, the redirect URL includes a combination of the two query strings. The query parameters from the **Redirect To** URL are appended to the query string in the request. For example, imagine your application receives a request for the relative path `/spring?year=2019`. If you’ve chosen to redirect `/spring` to `/summer?year=2020`, the redirect URL is `/summer?year=2019&year=2020` when forwarding is enabled. #### Forwarding Wildcard Path You can automatically include any path that comes after the wildcard portion of the **Redirect From** URL in the **Redirect To** URL. For example: if `/a/*` matches `/a/b/c` in the **Redirect From** URL, and the **Redirect To** URL is `/z/`, the redirect URL is `/z/b/c`. To enable wildcard path forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Wildcard Path**. ### Clone Redirects :::tip We recommend that you always create redirects in a staging environment and clone them into production after testing them. ::: You can copy all the redirects from one environment to another using the clone redirects feature. You can also clone redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_clone_create ](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_clone_create) API endpoint. To clone redirects using Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirects that you want to clone. 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 4. Click **Clone Redirects**. The **Clone Redirects** form appears. The current environment is listed under **From Environment** (the source). 5. Under **To Environment**, select the environment that you want to clone the redirects into (the destination). 6. Click **Clone n Redirects**. (Where n is the number of redirects to be cloned.) :::warning When you clone redirects, you’re replacing *all* the redirects in the destination environment with *all* the redirects from the source environment. ::: ### Edit a Redirect You can also edit a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_partial_update) API endpoint. To edit the settings for an existing redirect using Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to edit. 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 5. Click **Edit**. 6. Update the settings. 7. Click **Update Redirect**. ### Delete a Redirect You can also delete a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_destroy](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_destroy) API endpoint. To delete a redirect using Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to delete. 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 5. Click **Delete**. 6. Click **Yes, Delete Redirect**. ### Troubleshooting Redirects If a redirect isn’t working as expected, try these troubleshooting steps: - [Clear your browser cache](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop\&hl=en) because redirects are cached. - Verify that you’re viewing the settings for the correct environment. - Edit the redirect and verify that the correct values are entered in the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** fields. ### Technical Limitations with Redirects Redirects have the following technical limitations: - Each environment can have a maximum of 10,000 redirects. - Each environment has its own set of redirects. It is your responsibility to keep them in sync using cloning. - The redirects feature supports simple redirects from one path to another. For complex redirects with conditionals use Express.js' [redirects support](http://expressjs.com/en/api.html#res.redirect) in `ssr.js`. - Redirects created with the Runtime Admin tool or the Managed Runtime API are not run on local development environments. - Redirects are not triggered by page transitions in the PWA Kit application; they can only be triggered by an HTTP request. - To load a redirect in the context of a storefront, use the managed endpoint `/mobify/redirect/$path`. ## Users Here’s how to manage your users. ### Add a User To add a user to a project: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 3. Click **New User**. 4. Enter the user’s email address. (Make sure that the user is part of your organization and has either one of the following roles in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.) 5. Select a role. 6. Click **Add User**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-2.png) ### Change a User’s Role To change a user’s role: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 3. Click the **...** button next to the user’s name. 4. Click **Edit**. 5. Select a role. 6. Click the popup menu that appears. 7. Select a new role. 8. Click **Save**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-3.png) For a list of user abilities associated with each role, see the [Managed Runtime Overview](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/mrt-overview.md). ### Remove a User To remove a user from a project: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 3. Click the **...** button next to the user’s name. 4. Click **Remove**. 5. Click **Yes, Remove User**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-4.png)

The platform also has concrete limits: a maximum of 100 total environments per organization and 10 production environments, with the ability to request increases from Salesforce Support. Now I need to figure out how many environments Zimmermann currently uses across their projects to see if they're approaching these limits.

If Option B means creating a full 6-tier environment structure (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod) for each of the 18 integrations, that would require 108 total environments — already exceeding the 100-environment cap before even accounting for other projects. That's a major constraint that directly impacts Option B's viability and belongs in the TSD's constraints analysis. But I should reconsider whether every integration really needs all 6 tiers or if there's flexibility in how environments are structured across different apps. are free to create, relying on usage-based scaling infrastructure rather than per-environment licensing fees. However, the documentation doesn't clarify whether multiple projects themselves incur additional licensing costs — it only guarantees free environment creation within existing projects — so the actual per-project pricing likely depends on Zimmermann's specific Salesforce contract terms, which this generic product documentation doesn't address. The roles structure is critical here — each user gets exactly one project role with specific permissions like Deploy, Env Vars access, and team management. If we go with Option B (per-integration apps), we could assign different project roles to different squads for each integration, giving us genuine secrets isolation and control over who can deploy or access environment variables for which integration.

Under Option A with a single app, anyone with Developer or Admin role automatically gets access to ALL environment variables across ALL integrations — so a compromised credential for one integration becomes a blast radius problem affecting the entire platform. This is the concrete security argument that directly supports Option B's ownership and secrets isolation benefits.

Now I'm looking at the MRT execution and concurrency model to understand how failures propagate across integrations...

The App Server runs on serverless Node/Express infrastructure with horizontal auto-scaling, meaning resource exhaustion from one integration's slow calls wouldn't necessarily tank the entire environment — it'd be isolated to individual scaled instances rather than choking a single shared process.

However, this instance-level isolation doesn't protect against deploy-level blast radius: a code bug in a bad release would still affect ALL instances of that app since they all run the same bundle. So auto-scaling mitigates per-request resource contention to some degree, but not the risk of a broken deployment affecting the whole fleet.

There's also a hard platform constraint: App Server requests timeout at 20 seconds in production (16 seconds non-production) with an HTTP 502 response. This reinforces why per-integration timeouts matter — a slow call inside SSR could consume the entire request budget and timeout the whole page if not isolated with its own shorter deadline.

Additionally, unhandled promise rejections will break the entire app render, which is a critical platform-level constraint supporting both proper wiring of the existing undici pools and the failure-isolation argument for Option B — since all integrations run in the same Node process, a single unhandled rejection from one integration's code can cascade and break the entire page.

The deployment model confirms that bundles are environment-scoped and represent the entire PWA Kit app, so under Option A any integration change requires redeploying the whole bundle, meaning rolling back a single integration's bad change forces a full app rollback.  Option B sidesteps this by giving each integration its own app and bundle lineage, so a problematic deploy to one integration doesn't affect others at all. The immutability of bundles also aligns with the team's existing rollback workflow and troubleshooting practices.

Looking at the environment variables passed to the App Server — `DEPLOY_TARGET`, `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`, and `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID` — I can see that `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID` essentially maps to what the codebase refers to as the project slug. This confirms the mechanism I found earlier where the Explore agent uses `getProjectName()` from package.json to identify the project at push time, while the server assigns `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID` at runtime based on the project configuration.

Edge services like WAF, proxy, CDN, and edge functions are distributed geographically to serve users with minimal latency. Since these are configured per environment (or per project), choosing Option B with separate apps would mean duplicating this entire edge infrastructure setup for each app — adding operational complexity and maintenance overhead that's worth noting as a constraint.

There are also deployment bundle size limits to consider: the maximum is 400MB overall, with `ssr_only` and `ssr_shared` capped at 249MB. There are some infrastructure constraints around request/response sizes, the "/mobify" path prefix for managed endpoints, and AWS IP allowlisting for outbound traffic — these apply regardless of the topology choice, though Option B would require each app to negotiate allowlisting separately with integration partners rather than handling it centrally.

For the server-side rendering architecture, ARM is the default for new projects while x86 is being retired in January 2027, so I need to check whether the existing Zimmermann project runs on ARM or x86 — this could matter if Option B means creating entirely new projects that would automatically get the modern ARM setup.

On certificate management, TLS certs are organization-scoped resources that can be shared across projects within the same org, so Option B's multiple projects could all use the same wildcard certificate without needing separate provisioning for each app — this actually mitigates one of the potential downsides of splitting into multiple projects.

The key structural question that emerges from the project creation mechanics is whether a single Zimmermann codebase would need to be organized as a monorepo with multiple build targets each deploying to its own MRT project, or split into entirely separate repositories — this repo structure decision would be critical to nail down in the technical implementation section if Option B is chosen.

Option B does impose a one-time 40-minute deployment window per new project created, which is an operational cost but not a blocker. There's also the B2C CLI tooling available as an alternative to the traditional `pwa-kit-dev push` workflow, though this doesn't fundamentally shift the recommendation either way.

Looking at the user roles and permissions layer, Option B's project-level granularity (Admin/Developer/Marketer/Viewer) is a significant security advantage — it lets you restrict who can deploy, view environment variables, or access logs on a per-integration basis, whereas Option A forces broad access to anyone who needs to touch any integration. That said, there's a nuance: org-level MRT access (granted via Account Manager role) is still organization-wide, so the real isolation comes from deliberately not assigning someone a project role rather than a hard technical barrier preventing them from being added to a project they shouldn't access.

The redirects section hints at an operational complexity for Option B: since each environment maintains its own redirect rules and they need manual syncing, a global redirect requirement would mean cloning that rule across multiple separate projects instead of managing it in one place — though this assumes redirects are storefront-URL-level rather than integration-specific, which they actually are since they govern user-facing URLs, not backend integration calls.

This raises a deeper architectural question: does splitting into per-integration MRT apps mean the customer-facing SSR rendering stays centralized in one app while backend integration code moves to separate apps, or does it mean literally splitting the entire application stack per integration?

The key insight is that MRT apps are fundamentally HTTP-serving units — each one responds to requests based on its own domain/hostname, so every MRT app is a complete request-handling instance.

If you wanted to split the storefront by integration (one app per payment provider, for example), you'd face a critical architectural problem: you'd need to either fragment the routing across multiple separate apps/domains, or put a reverse proxy in front of them. But the existing architecture depends on all storefronts living under a single first-party domain so they can share session cookies — splitting them into separate apps would break that session-sharing mechanism entirely.

The workaround would be to keep the integration apps as internal backend services that the main storefront app calls via HTTP, rather than trying to route shoppers directly to them. That way, the shopper only ever visits the main storefront domain, and the integration apps remain invisible backend services.

Alternatively, there's a simpler middle ground: stick with a single app but structure it modularly. This constraint about one hostname per MRT environment is the key insight that makes the per-integration-app approach problematic — each app would need its own environment and hostname, but then I'd need to layer DNS or CDN routing on top to make it transparent to users, which adds complexity and potential failure points that the single modular app approach avoids entirely. Both approaches require meaningful infrastructure work — either server-to-server calls between MRT projects (routing through the public internet like existing MuleSoft integrations) or external CDN-level path routing across multiple origins. This analysis from the new docs clarifies that Option B's infrastructure complexity is substantial and should significantly weigh the TSD's evaluation of trade-offs.

The elegant insight here is that the existing undici-pool pattern already provides the exact mechanism needed: treating sibling MRT "integration apps" as third-party backend services with their own connection pools, timeouts, and configuration — meaning wiring up the undici pools (a known gap) becomes valuable regardless of which topology wins, since it's the foundation Option B would rely on for inter-MRT communication.

Now I'm pinning down the platform constraints for the TSD: orgs can have up to 100 total environments with 10 marked as production (raisable through Salesforce Support), and Zimmermann currently uses 6 environments across one project. If Option B scaled to one app per integration system across ~18 systems, that would be 18 projects × 6 environments = 108 total environments — already exceeding the 100-environment org cap before even accounting for additional projects.

This hard constraint makes the extreme "one MRT app per integration" approach impractical at scale, but a middle-ground strategy grouping related integrations into 3-5 domain-focused apps (like a payments app covering Adyen, GiveX, and reCAPTCHA, or a CRM app for MuleSoft, Omneo, and Booxi) would consume far fewer environments and stay within limits.

This is a concrete, quantifiable finding that should shape the options analysis and recommendation. Now I need to revisit whether this new information fully addresses Task #2 about MRT supporting multiple independent applications in the organization.

The architectural support is definitively confirmed through official documentation—the org→projects→environments hierarchy explicitly allows multiple projects. On the cost model side, I've found that environments themselves carry no additional cost to create up to the numeric limits since they run on auto-scaling serverless infrastructure, but this comes from Salesforce's general platform documentation rather than a Zimmermann-specific contract statement. So I've answered the architectural question, though the cost model piece remains partially unresolved without seeing their actual invoice or contract terms. The commercial side still needs confirmation from the account team, but the platform capabilities are now fully locked down. I've got concrete numbers for all the limits — 100 total environments with 10 production max per org, 400MB bundle size, 6MB request limit, 10240-byte headers, 20-second execution timeout, 250 IP allowlist entries, and 10000 redirects per environment — all quotable for the constraints section. The concurrency and execution model is also confirmed now. Provisioning additional MRT projects is purely a commercial question with Zimmermann, and checking the architecture (ARM vs x86) for their existing project is straightforward via Runtime Admin UI—something Marcel likely has access to themselves as a repo admin. The last piece is confirming how many environments Zimmermann's currently using against the org-wide 100/10 capacity limits.

This is a major breakthrough—those two docs have essentially resolved all the previously-existential blockers that seemed Gideon-only. What remains are just narrow items: the commercial cost discussion and two quick Runtime Admin checks that don't require special access. I need to update the SFCC-237 memory file to reflect this substantial unblock and make it clear to the user how much ground we've actually covered.

For the task tracker, I should mark Task #2 and Task #3 as substantially resolved via documentation, with only minor residual items remaining—either closing them with a note about what's left, or spinning off a smaller follow-up task for the narrow commercial/account-specific confirmations. I need to be careful here—the user's instruction is specifically asking for analysis, not for me to jump into drafting the TSD. They've established a clear pattern of wanting to control the pacing, so I should present the findings from these new docs, confirm how they resolve the blockers, and report back rather than getting ahead of myself with the actual recommendation document.

I also need to flag the nuance around cost modeling: while the docs clarify that environments are free to create, they don't fully address project-level costs, so I shouldn't overclaim that this blocker is completely resolved. And the single-domain architectural constraint I spotted is genuinely important—I should present it clearly but concisely. I'm also noticing the bundle size limits got cut off mid-sentence, so I'll need to pull that complete information to present accurately. ous ceiling unlikely to be hit.

The rollback mechanism aligns with what the team already uses in their Managed Runtime Console—it's just re-designating a previous bundle as deployed for that environment. And since TLS certificates are org-scoped and usable across any environment, that's another constraint worth factoring into the deploy/rollback scoring dimension.

## Open items — MOSTLY RESOLVED 2026-08-10 via official MRT platform docs

User supplied `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/mrt-overview.md` + `mrt-administration.md` (official
Salesforce Managed Runtime docs). These resolve almost everything that previously required a
Gideon/platform conversation:

**Multi-app support — CONFIRMED YES.** "An organization can contain multiple projects for
multiple storefronts and each project can contain multiple environments" (mrt-overview.md
"Projects and Organizations"). Platform-architecturally, Option B is fully supported — this was
the single biggest open unknown and it's now closed.

**Numeric platform limits — CONFIRMED, and this is a real constraint on Option B's *shape*.**
Org-wide cap: **max 100 total environments, max 10 production environments** (raisable only by
contacting Salesforce Support). Zimmermann today uses 6 environments (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/
prod) in one project. A literal "one MRT app per integration" reading of Option B (~18 systems ×
6 tiers = 108 environments) **exceeds the 100-environment org cap on its own** and would need a
Support-ticket limit increase for production count too. A **domain-grouped** version (e.g. 3-5
apps clustering related integrations — payments, CMS-proxy, CRM/order-data, etc.) stays
comfortably under both caps (~24-36 total environments). This is the first hard, quantified
argument for why Option B, if chosen, should group by domain rather than by individual
integration — feed directly into §2.1 Constraints and §3 Options Analysis.

**Cost model — PARTIALLY resolved, nuance matters.** "Because environments run on highly
efficient microservices that automatically scale up and down, you can create as many
environments as you need **at no additional cost**" (up to the caps above). This answers the
*platform-mechanics* half (environments aren't individually metered) but is generic Salesforce
product documentation, not a Zimmermann-specific commercial statement — it does **not** confirm
whether Zimmermann's actual contract caps or charges for an *additional project* (as opposed to
additional environments within an existing project). **Narrowed remaining open item:** confirm
with account team/Gideon whether provisioning a wholly new MRT *project* (not just an
environment) has any commercial implication under Zimmermann's specific agreement.

**MRT execution/concurrency model — CONFIRMED.** App Server = Node.js + Express, "serverless,"
auto-scaling ("massive scaling capacity"). Critically: **"Unhandled promise rejections break app
rendering"** (mrt-overview.md, Rendering constraints) — this is the concrete platform-level
mechanism behind the failure-isolation argument: under Option A, one integration's unhandled
rejection can break rendering for a request that also needed a *different*, otherwise-healthy
integration, because they share the same Node process/request lifecycle. Hard execution-time
ceiling: **20s production / 16s non-production**, then HTTP 502 — a real ceiling regardless of
topology, and a concrete reason the still-inert undici per-pool timeouts (`connectionPools.ts`,
see Discrepancy #2) matter independent of which option wins.

**Deploy/rollback granularity — CONFIRMED, directly answers the ticket's named dimension.**
"Each project can have multiple bundles, but each environment can have only one bundle designated
as deployed" — a bundle is the *entire* built app, immutable. **Under Option A, any change to any
one integration requires deploying (and, if bad, rolling back) the single shared bundle
containing all integrations' code** — a bad change to Integration X forces a rollback that also
reverts unrelated Integration Y's code if it shipped in the same bundle. Option B gives each
domain-app its own independent bundle lineage — true deploy/rollback isolation. This is the
clearest, most concrete win for Option B of everything found so far.

**Architectural catch for Option B — new insight, important for §3 Options Analysis.** MRT
environments are hostname-bound HTTP-serving units ("A hostname can be set as the External
Hostname for only one environment at a time"). Zimmermann's architecture.md §"Cross-Storefront
Session & Basket Scope" depends on **all 8 storefronts sharing one first-party domain** for
session-cookie sharing. A literal per-integration-app split would need either (a) each
integration-app treated as an **internal backend microservice** that the one customer-facing
"front door" app calls server-to-server (exactly the pattern the still-inert `connectionPools.ts`
undici pools were designed for — this becomes the actual wiring mechanism, not just a nice-to-have),
or (b) CDN/edge-level path routing across multiple MRT origins (heavier — Zimmermann's CDN is
Akamai/SFCC-default per architecture.md, not something MRT's own per-project edge covers across
projects). **This means "per-integration app" in practice is a backend-microservices-behind-one-
front-door pattern, not a literal request-routing split** — worth stating explicitly in the TSD
so Option B isn't misread as "split the storefront itself into 18 sites."

**Certificates — a non-issue either way.** TLS certs are **org-scoped**, usable by any environment
in the same org (not per-project) — Option B's extra projects would share the same wildcard cert
with no additional certificate-provisioning overhead.

**Project-level role granularity — a concrete secrets/ownership-blast-radius argument for Option
B.** Each MRT project has its own Admin/Developer/Marketer/Viewer role assignments (env-var
visibility, deploy access, log access are all project-scoped, one role per user per project).
Under Option A everyone who needs deploy/env-var access to *any* integration necessarily has it
for *all* integrations (one shared project). Option B lets access be scoped per domain-app —
directly answers the ticket's "secrets & security blast radius" and "ownership" dimensions with a
platform-verified mechanism, not a hypothetical.

**Collateral finding (out of SFCC-237's scope — one-TSD-one-problem — but worth flagging
separately):** "Server-Side Cookie Access is enabled by default for new projects. **Existing
projects continue to have server-side cookies turned off by default**" (mrt-administration.md).
Zimmermann's `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie architecture (architecture.md §"Cross-Storefront
Session") is load-bearing on server-side cookie access being *on*. Worth an independent Runtime
Admin check (project settings) that this is actually enabled on the existing `zimmermann` project
— not something derivable from the codebase, and not something to fold into this TSD.

**Now genuinely narrow remaining opens (all "check Runtime Admin," not "unknowable platform
questions"):** (1) Zimmermann's actual commercial cost for an *additional project* specifically;
(2) current environment/production-count usage against the 100/10 org caps, to know real headroom;
(3) whether the existing `zimmermann` project runs ARM or x86 (x86 retires 2027-01-31; ARM is
default for anything created after its introduction); (4) the server-side-cookie collateral check
above. None of these require Claude — they're one-glance-at-Runtime-Admin facts for whoever has
access (the user has Managed Runtime access per role, presumably).
